[Summary] Jongno Jewelry Shopping Street, located in Jongno, a central district of Seoul, is well known nationwide. It is estimated to house between 2,000 and 4,000 jewelry stores of every size and packed close together in one district.
[Description] Jongno Jewelry Shopping Street, located in Jongno, a central district of Seoul, is well known nationwide. It is estimated to house between 2,000 and 4,000 jewelry stores of every size and packed close together in one district. Jongno district has always had a large floating population and has been a well-developed commercial area since olden times. The jewelry street in its current form has existed since the 1960s. Even though the area has repeatedly undergone major changes to its academic and entertainment venues, the jewelry street continues to be as lively as ever. At present, about 70 percent of the domestic jewelry market is traded on Jongno Jewelry Shopping Street. The first thing that catches the eye is the number of wholesale and retail stores lining the street (Jongnodaero), which now form a new commercial zone in the area. Here, customers can purchase jewelry at around 20 to 40 percent cheaper than market prices, since most stores have close connections with jewelry-makers and can lower prices. Proof of this is the number of gold-and-silver workshops nearby, in an area slightly bigger than 3.3 square meters. Jewelry Street is especially popular with lovers and soon-to-be-married couples, and overseas tourists frequently visit looking for Korean jewelry at low prices.

[설명] 서울에서 가장 스타일리시한 골목, 삼청동. 언제부터인가 가난한 예술가들이 삼청동으로 찾아들었습니다. 거리에 예술적 향취가 묻어나기 시작했고, 지금의 삼청동 거리가 만들어졌습니다. 골목길 구석구석에 보물같이 예쁜 가게들이 숨어 있지만 중심 거리 양쪽으로 늘어선 색색의 쇼윈도 먼저 구경해보세요. 재기발랄한 인테리어 숍이 눈을 끄는가 하면 바로 옆 가게에는 고풍스러운 전통숍이 자리 잡고 있는데 서로 훌륭한 조화를 이룹니다. 거리를 거니는 사람들도 무척 다채롭습니다. 카페를 배경 삼아 사진을 찍는 젊은이들, 한옥 갤러리에서 작품을 감상하는 이들, 이색 박물관에서 다양한 전시품을 감상하는 가족 단위 관람객들이 모두 같은 길에서 호흡합니다. 메마른 감성을 충전시키고 발길 닿는 집에 들어가 맛난 음식을 즐길 수도 있는 곳, 삼청동은 바로 그런 동네입니다.

[Summary] Samcheongdong is Seoul's most stylish neighborhood, located just past Gyeongbokgung (Palace)'s stone wall lined street.
[Description] Samcheongdong is Seoul's most stylish neighborhood, located just past Gyeongbokgung Palace's stone wall lined street. The name "Samcheong" is derived from the words "sam" meaning “three", and "cheong" meaning "fresh" or "pure", because the mountain, water and the heart of the people in this area are all very fresh and pure. Then it's not wonder why many artists have sought out Samcheong-dong over the years. Because of this, Samcheong-dong became known as an artistic area. The area of Samcheongdong is actually made up of several neighborhoods: Anguk-dong, Sogyeok-dong, Hwa-dong, and Sagan-dong and ends at Samcheong Park. Samcheong-dong is dotted with various art museums, museums, art galleries, restaurants, cafés, and shops; some are traditional, some are modern, but all are unique and colorful.

[요약] 한강 위에서 서울의 야경과 낭만을 즐길 수 있는 특별한 유람선 체험
[설명] 한강을 즐기기에 가장 좋은 방법은 바로 유람선입니다. 시원한 강바람을 맞으며 한강 양쪽의 경치를 모두 감상할 수 있기 때문입니다. 한강의 낮과 밤 풍경을 충분히 즐길 수 있도록, 다양한 시간대의 크루즈가 준비되어있습니다. '한강 투어 크루즈'는 매일 낮시간에 운행되는 크루즈로, 라이브 공연을 즐기며 서울의 도심을 구경할 수 있습니다. 매일 오후 6시에는 '선셋 크루즈'가 운행되어 로맨틱한 노을을 감상할 수 있고, 저녁과 밤 시간대에는 '달빛 뮤직 크루즈'와 '별빛 크루즈'가 운행되어 선상에서 아름다운 한강의 야경을 바라볼 수 있습니다. 이외에도 화려한 불꽃놀이를 함께 즐기는 불꽃 뮤직 크루즈, 뷔페나 샴폐인을 곁들이는 디너 크루즈도 마련되어있습니다. 새빛 둥둥섬, 노들섬, 여의도, 국회의사당, 잠실 등 서울 곳곳의 명소를 선상에서 라이브 음악을 감상하며 즐길 수 있습니다. 연인, 친구, 가족들과 함께 오붓한 시간을 보내기에도 좋고, 혼자 방문하여 사색을 즐기는 시간을 갖기에도 좋습니다. 코스 별로 운항 정보가 상이하므로 자세한 내용은 홈페이지를 참고하는 것을 추천합니다.

[Place] Hangang Eland Cruise
[Category] Experience Programs > Other Experiences
[Summary] One of the best ways to enjoy the Hangang River.
[Description] The ultimate way to experience the Hangang River is by embarking on a cruise. Feel the refreshing breeze as you enjoy the picturesque views along both banks. Various cruises are available day and night, allowing you to appreciate the river’s beauty in a different light. The "Hangang Tour Cruise" runs daily during the day, offering a chance to explore Seoul's cityscape while enjoying live entertainment. Every evening at 6 PM, the "Sunset Cruise" provides a romantic view of the setting sun. For those who prefer evening or night outings, the "Moonlight Music Cruise" and "Starlight Cruise" offer stunning nighttime views of the Hangang River. Special options like the "Fireworks Music Cruise," featuring dazzling displays, and the "Dinner Cruise," which includes a buffet or champagne, add an extra luxury to your river experience. Aboard the cruise, you can enjoy live music while soaking in the sights of Seoul's iconic landmarks, including Sebitseom Island, Nodeul Island, Yeouido, the National Assembly Building, and Jamsil. It’s an ideal way to spend quality time with a partner, friends, or family, and offers a serene setting for those who wish to enjoy some peaceful reflection alone. Since schedules and routes vary by course, checking the official website for detailed information is advisable.
[Tags] Ferry, Hangang, Cruise, Cruise, Eland, Seoul

[Description] Olympic Park was originally built for the 1988 Seoul Olympic Games and nowadays offers Seoulites a wide range of cultural, sporting and leisure opportunities.Olympic Park is divided into four zones: arts and culture, recreation and sport, environment and history. [Place] Maeheon Citizens’ Forest
[Category] Culture > Parks
[Summary] Yangjae Citizens’ Forest is a lush public park located in Yangjae-dong.
[Description] Located in Yangjae-dong, Seocho-gu, Seoul, Maeheon Citizen's Forest is the first park in South Korea to introduce the concept of a forest, featuring a dense woodland rarely seen in urban areas. Established in 1986 to improve the environment around the Yangjae Tollgate, then a gateway to Seoul, in preparation for the 1986 Asian Games and the 1988 Olympics, this park offers various facilities such as a lawn plaza, floor fountain, pergolas, volleyball court, basketball court, and tennis courts, ensuring residents' health and relaxation through free activities in nature. Additionally, the park houses the Maehun Yun Bonggil Memorial Hall and, to the south, significant historical monuments such as the Memorial Tower of Baengmagoji Battlefield, Korean Air Flight 858 Memorial, and the Sampoong Department Store Memorial, encapsulating key moments of modern Korean history.

[Summary] Yeouido Park is a large public park near the Hangang River that is popular for its sporting and leisure options as well as its cherry blossoms.
[Description] Opened in 1971 on the site of a former runway, Yeouido Park is a civic park located in Yeouido-dong, Yeongdeungpo-gu, Seoul. The park comprises four distinct areas: the Korean Traditional Forest, the Culture Plaza, the Grass Field, and the Ecological Forest. It features bike paths and walking trails around its perimeter, serving as a space for relaxation and cultural activities for residents. Various seasonal programs are offered throughout the year, and it is advisable to check the park's website for details. Yeouido Park highlights recommended routes for enjoying its notable landmarks and natural scenery. An exhibition hall featuring a C-47 aircraft stands on the spot where, three days after Korea's liberation, the Korean Liberation Army's Jeongjindae unit landed in collaboration with the American OSS unit.

[Description] The Amsa-dong Prehistoric Settlement Site is a historic site where visitors can learn about Korea during the Neolithic era. [Place] Mongchontoseong Fortress
[Category] History > Historical Sites > Fortresses & Gates
[Summary] Mongchontoseong Fortress is the remains of earthen fortifications from the Baekje Period and was built around the 3rd or 4th century.
[Description] Mongchontoseong Fortress is the remains of earthen fortifications from the Baekje Period and was built around the 3rd or 4th century. The fortress is located within Olympic Park and its circumference is approximately 2.7km in total. There is a 2.4km walking trail that is open to the public. The Mongchontoseong Museum of History is located with the circumference of the fortress and the museum features dugout hut sites dating back to the beginning of Baekje Dynasty, as well as artifacts discovered during excavations. Admission to Mongchontoseong Fortress is free.

[Place] Banpodaegyo Bridge Moonlight Rainbow Fountain
[Category] Culture > Landmarks
[Summary] The world’s longest bridge fountain (recognized by the Guinness Book of World Records) with 380 water jets and a dazzling array of multi-colored lights.
[Description] Banpodaegyo Bridge is a two-tiered bridge over the Han River that features the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain, (the world’s longest bridge fountain recognized by the Guinness Book of World Records) with 380 water jets and a dazzling array of multi-colored lights. The Moonlight Rainbow Fountain’s water jets are dynamic and can move in time to music creating spectacular ever-changing displays. Add to that the hundreds of rainbow-colored lighting combinations when night falls, and it is easy to see why Banpodaegyo Bridge is a magnet for tourists year round. The Moonlight Rainbow Fountain operates from April to October every year, however the schedule of the fountain shows varies from month to month. Each fountain show lasts 20 minutes. In addition, Banpo Hangang Park hosts the "Moonlight Square Cultural Weekend" event every Saturday from 7:00 - 8:30 p.m. from May to October, featuring a variety of musical styles including classical music with commentary, acappella, popera, jazz, brass bands and orchestras. [Summary] Ilmin Museum of Art is a private art museum that mainly exhibits Korean contemporary art.
[Description] Ilmin Museum of Art is a private art museum that mainly exhibits Korean contemporary art. It was originally established to commemorate Kim Sangman, former president of the Donga Ilbo, one of Korea's leading media outlets. The museum's name was taken from Kim's pen name, Ilmin (meaning “one people” or “a nation united” in Korean). The museum is run by the Ilmin Cultural Foundation and a variety of special exhibitions and art classes are held throughout the year. The museum has a cafe and restaurant on the first floor.

[Description] Bulgwangcheon Stream, which originates in Bulgwang-dong, Eunpyeong-gu, flows through Yeokchon-dong, Eungam-dong, and Jeungsan-dong, and extends to Bukgajwa-dong in Seodaemun-gu and Seongsan-dong in Mapo-gu, covering a length of approximately 9.21 km. In 2002, wastewater prevention facilities were installed, and groundwater was pumped to create the current flowing stream. Named after the nearby Bulgwangsa Temple, the upper stream of Bulgwangcheon Stream features riverside stands and fountain shows. Along the stream are well-developed bike paths and walking trails, with various trees and aquatic plants offering diverse landscaping throughout the seasons. This restored ecosystem makes Bulgwangcheon Stream a beloved walking path for residents.

[설명] 지하철 1,7호선 가산디지털단지역(구 가리봉역) 4번 출구로 나오면 마리오아울렛, 더블유몰(W-Mall), 오렌지아울렛 등의 쇼핑센터를 중심으로 유명 브랜드 할인매장이 다양하게 모여 있는 것을 볼 수 있습니다. 가리봉로데오 쇼핑의 매력은 초대형 아울렛 매장이 많다는 것입니다. 20~30대 여성들이 가장 많이 찾는 마리오 아울렛에는 폴로 랄프로렌부터 노티카, 타미힐피거, 버버리 등 국내외 유명 브랜드가 대부분 입점해 있습니다. 더블유몰은 층마다 고객층을 달리하는 백화점식 매장 구성으로 눈길을 끕니다. 세련된 다지인의 매장들은 대부분의 제품을 60~70% 세일합니다. 길 건너편에 위치한 모피매장도 인기입니다. 진도모피, 엘페, 진도옴므, 우바 등을 일반매장에 비해 5% 이상 추가 할인합니다. 만승아울렛은 나이키부터 필라, 아디다스 등 스포츠 의류 매장이 많습니다. 영업시간은 오전 10시 30분부터 밤 9시까지로 연중 무휴입니다 .

[Description] Hongjecheon Stream is the first tributary of the Hangang River. The stream runs 13.92km-long and flows through Jongno-gu, Seodaemun-gu and Mapo-gu. [Place] Taereung and Gangreung Royal Tombs
[Category] History > Historical Sites > Tombs & Mausoleums
[Summary] Taereung and Gangneung Royal Tombs are the burial sites of royalty from the Joseon Dynasty.
[Description] Taereung and Gangneung Royal Tombs are the burial sites of royalty from the Joseon Dynasty. Located in Hwarang-dong, Taereung and Gangneung sit next to each other. The Korea National Training Center for Sports sits between the two royal tombs and the center is operated by the Korean Olympic Committee. Taereung is the royal tomb of Queen Munjeong; the second wife of the 11th Joseon king, Jungjong. Gangneung is the royal tomb of the Queen Munjeong's son and the 13th Joseon king, Myeongjong and his wife, Queen Insun. In June 2009, all 40 of the royal tombs of the Joseon Dynasty were designated UNESCO World Heritage sites.

[요약] 아시아를 대표하는 아라리오 갤러리. 서울, 천안, 중국 상하이에 운영
[설명] 아라리오갤러리는 그동안 다른 갤러리가 시도하지 않았던 해외 미술과의 적극적인 연계로 한국 미술계에 혼성성과 다양성을 이끌어내었을 뿐 아니라, 지속적이고 체계적인 전속작가 시스템을 도입하여 한국의 동시대 미술을 해외에 소개하는데 앞장서 왔습니다. 현재는 중국 미술계에서의 경험을 토대로 국내에 소개된 바 없는 인도 및 동남아시아 작가들의 다양한 작품세계를 한국 미술계에 소개합니다. 나아가 지속적인 프로모션을 통해 이들 지역의 신진작가를 발굴 및 후원하고 있습니다. 아라리오갤러리는 우수한 전속작가 시스템과 다양한 국, 내외 미술관과의 콜라보레이션, 다양한 해외지역 미술의 소개 등을 토대로 한국과 미술의 가능성을 확장하고 마켓을 선도하는 아시아 대표 갤러리로서 그 역할을 다할 것입니다. 아라리오갤러리 서울은 2006년 종로구 소격동에서 첫 문을 연 이래 탄탄한 전속 작가 시스템과 과감한 전시 기획력을 발판으로 동시대 미술현장을 이끌어 가고 있습니다. 2014년 3월 국립현대미술관 인근으로 위치를 이전하였으며, 2018년 4월부터 2019년 11월까지는 홍익대학교 인근에 서울의 두 번째 전시공간인 아라리오갤러리 서울 라이즈호텔을 열어 지역이 상징하는 젊고 새로운 실험정신을 계승, 발전시키고자 노력하기도 하였습니다. 2022년 아라리오갤러리 서울은 소격동 시대를 종료한 후 2023년 2월 종로구 원서동에서 한층 새로운 모습으로 재개관하였습니다. 선제적 발굴 및 꾸준한 지원을 통해 작가들의 조력자로 활동하고 함께 성장하는 데 목표를 둠과 동시에 실험적이며 진지한 전시 기획을 실현시켜 한국 미술계의 발전에 지속적으로 도움이 되고자 합니다.

[Place] Arario Gallery Seoul
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Art Museums/Galleries
[Summary] The Arario Gallery is one of Seoul's renowned art galleries. New or prominent, Korean or international, the gallery exhibits the best there is.
[Description] Over the years, Arario Gallery Seoul has led the way in curating a harmonic fusion and variety of different art forms in Korea's art community through bold collaborations with international artistry that have never been attempted before. Also, the gallery takes the forefront in introducing artwork from today's more modern Korean artists having implemented an ongoing and structured system of exclusively-contracted artists. Currently, a wide range of artworks from artists native to India and Southeast Asia, who have yet to come to Korea despite having already experienced China's art community, are finally getting some spotlight in Korea. What's better is that with the help of continued promotional activity, the search and funding for up-and-coming talent in the respective regions is ongoing as well. Thanks to the gallery's efforts grounded in a system of exclusive artists displaying excellence; various collaborations with other galleries, both at home and abroad; introductions of varied artworks from numerous places around the world; and more, the Arario Gallery is set to play out its role as Asia's signature gallery that expands upon the possibilities for the future of Korea's art community while leading the market as well.

Since its first opening in Sogyeok-dong, Jongno-gu, in 2006, Arario Gallery Seoul has been leading the contemporary art scene based on its solid artist system and bold exhibition planning capabilities. In March 2014, it relocated near the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, and from April 2018 to November 2019, Arario Gallery Seoul Ryse Hotel, its second exhibition space in Seoul, opened near Hongik University. This effort aimed to inherit and develop the youthful and innovative spirit symbolized by the area. In 2022, Arario Gallery Seoul ended its Sogyeok-dong era and reopened with a new look in Wonseo-dong, Jongno-gu, in February 2023. The gallery aims to collaborate and support artists, striving for mutual growth through proactive exploration and consistent support. At the same time, it seeks to realize experimental and serious exhibition planning to continuously contribute to the advancement of the Korean art scene.

[Place] Yangjaecheon Stream & Tancheon Stream
[Category] Nature > Natural Sites(Rivers)
[Summary] Yangjaecheon Stream and Tancheon Stream are two tributaries of the Hangang River. The streams offer picturesque walking trails for visitors to enjoy.
[Description] Yangjaecheon Stream and Tancheon Stream are two tributaries of the Hangang River. The streams offer picturesque walking trails for visitors to enjoy. Yangjaecheon Stream, sometimes referred to as Hanyeoul Stream, is a tributary of the Hangang River. The stream is 18.5 km long and flows from Gwacheong in Gyeonggi-do Province to the southern part of Seoul. The stream's name is derived from the area in Seoul it flows through, Yangjae-dong. Tancheon Stream is another one of the Hangang's tributaries. The stream is 35.6 km long and starts in the city of Yongin in Gyeonggi-do Province and ends at the Hangang River in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. With its gently sloping walking paths and well-maintained cycling routes stretching along the stream, this urban waterway is a popular spot for walking, running, and riding. It is especially famous as a tourist destination for cherry blossoms in spring and colorful foliage in autumn.

document_title: A Look at Yonsei University's 3 Historic Halls
document_text:
[Place] A Look at Yonsei University's 3 Historic Halls
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Museums
[Summary] Yonsei University is one of Korea's best universities. Its history is deep and many of the buildings on the Yonsei campus have modern historical significance.
[Description] Yonsei University is one of Korea's best universities. Its history is deep and many of the buildings on the Yonsei campus have modern historical significance as they were built in the early years of the 20th century. Stimson Hall was the first building ever built on the Yonsei campus and it was constructed in 1920. The hall was designated Historic Site No. 275 in 1981. Underwood Hall, Historic Site No. 276, was the second building ever built at Yonsei University. Today the hall functions as a museum dedicated to the founder of Yonsei, Horace G. Underwood and the Underwood family. Appenzeller Hall was built in 1924 and holds the designation of Historic Site No. 277. The hall was built to commemorate Henry Appenzeller who established the famed Korean boys' school, Paichai Hakdang.

[Place] Bangi-dong Ancient Baekje Tombs
[Category] History > Historical Sites > Tombs & Mausoleums
[Summary] The Bangi-dong Ancient Baekje Tombs are ancient tombs in located the Bangi-dong area that date back to the Hanseong Baekje era.
[Description] The Bangi-dong Ancient Baekje Tombs are ancient tombs in located the Bangi-dong area that date back to the Hanseong Baekje era. The ancient Hanseong Baekje Kingdom was founded along the Hangang River in 18 BCE and lasted for nearly 5 centuries. The tombs were discovered in the 1970s during the Jamsil District Zoning Project and there are 8 tombs altogether. Unfortunately, most of the artifacts were stolen at some point in time, but the tombs themselves were preserved well. Visitors can observe the original structures of the tombs and learn more about Hanseong Baekje. These ancient tombs are an important historical site and the area around the tombs was made into a park. There are paths between the tombs and visitors can take a quiet walk around the park and observe the tombs while enjoying the park's fresh air and grass. The site holds the designation of Historic Site No. 270.

[Category] History > Religious Sites
[Summary] Jogyesa Temple is one of Korea's major Buddhist temples in central Seoul.
[Description] Jogyesa Temple was established in 1910 under the name Gakhwangsa by monks who aspired for the independence of Korean Buddhism and the restoration of the national capital. At the time, Gakhwangsa was the first temple to be situated within the four main gates of Seoul. In 1937, efforts began to relocate Gakhwangsa to its present site, now known as Jogyesa. Positioned in the heart of Jongno, Seoul, it is the only traditional temple in the city center, offering a place for visitors to rest. The temple grounds are open 24/7, welcoming locals and foreigners anytime. The temple hosts a temple stay program and the annual Lotus Lantern Festival.

[설명] 2002년, 선사 시대부터 현대까지 서울의 역사와 문화를 정리하여 보여줄 서울역사박물관이 경희궁터에 문을 열었습니다. 열린 박물관이 모토인 만큼 다른 박물관들에 비해 개방적입니다. 공간과 전시가 기존의 방 중심에서 벗어나 마당 중심의 개방적 체계로 구성되었습니다. 또한 체험 중심적입니다. 복제 유물을 전시하여 직접 만져보면서 유물에 대한 영상 정보를 볼 수 있는 '터치 뮤지엄 코너'를 운영하고 있습니다. 서울역사박물관에서 가장 먼저 둘러볼 곳은 역시 상설전시장입니다. 서울의 이모저모는 유서 깊은 서울의 역사와 전통문화를 정리하여 보여줌으로써 서울에 대한 이해와 역사의식을 심어주고 있습니다. 서울역사박물관은 서울의 대표적 문화 중심이 되어 서울 시민 및 서울을 찾는 내외국인들에게 서울의 문화를 느끼고 체험하는 기회를 제공하고 있습니다.

[Place] The Seoul Museum of History
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Museums
[Summary] The Seoul Museum of History is the only museum in Korea that represents the city’s 600 years of history and culture through interactive exhibitions.
[Description] The Seoul Museum of History is the only museum in Korea that represents the city’s history and culture. Since its establishment on the former site of Gyeonghuigung Palace in 2002, the museum has offered visitors the chance to experience 600 years of Seoul’shistoryand culture through interactive exhibitions. The three-story museum is divided thematically into three exhibition areas, including a special exhibition area, a permanent exhibition area and a hall that exhibits collections donated by the public. The museum offers accessible and interactive exhibitions to the public with various hands-on programs. [설명] 시민들의 휴식 공간, 연인들의 데이트 공간으로 널리 사랑받는 한강시민공원 잠원 지구는 다양한 수상 스포츠 시설과 8.2킬로미터에 달하는 인라인 스케이트 도로로 잘 알려져 있습니다. 또한 돗자리 깔고 누워 시간 보내기 좋은 폭신한 잔디밭이 넓게 펼쳐지고 반포 지구까지 자전거길이 이어져 있어 자전거를 타는 이들도 자주 찾는 곳입니다. 특히 장애인 전용 테니스장도 있어 시민들에게 꾸준한 사랑을 받고 있습니다. 잠원동은 조선시대부터 일제강점기까지 대규모 뽕밭이들어섰던 곳입니다. 이에 서울시 한강사업본부는 어린이들에게 지역의 역사를 알리기 위해 잠원 지구에 누에의 일생을 형상화한 테마 자연 학습관 ‘잠원 자연 학습장’을 개장했습니다. 자연 학습장은 진입마당, 누에전시마당, 자생초화원, 학습마당 등으로 구성되어 있으며, 다양한 체험 코스가 마련되어 있습니다.

[Place] Jamwon Hangang Park
[Category] Nature > Natural Sites(Rivers)
[Summary] Acts as both a popular date spot, as well as home to numerous sports facilities, including 8.2 km inline skating rink.
[Description] A famous relaxing spot for locals and beloved dating spot for couples, Jamwon Hangang Park is well-known for its numerous sports facilities and 8.2 km inline skating rink. Featuring wide grassy fields perfect for picnics, a bike path stretching all the way to Banpo District, and also a tennis court for the disabled, Jamwon Hangang Park continues to attract many visitors. From the Joseon Dynasty to the Japanese Occupation, the area of Jamwon-dong was a large-scale mulberry field. To educate future generations about the history of this area, Seoul Metropolitan Government opened up a "Jamwon Nature Learning Center." The learning center consists of a lobby, silkworm exhibition hall, wildflower garden, and classrooms, offering various experience programs for children.

[Description] Kukkiwon is the official headquarters for the Korean martial art of Taekwondo. At Kukkiwon, practitioners of Taekwondo can become certified instructors, undergo tests to climb the ranks, and attend the institute's Taekwondo academy. Another of Kukkiwon's aims is to develop and promote awareness of Taekwondo as a sport and as part of Korea's cultural heritage. Frequently Asked Questions about Kukkiwon What are the opening hours and admission fees for the Kukkiwon (World Taekwondo Headquarters)? The Kukkiwon (World Taekwondo Headquarters) is open from 9 am to 5:30 pm from Monday to Friday. It is closed for lunch from 11:30 am to 1:00 pm. Admission is free and it is closed on public holidays, national holidays, and Kukkiwon closed days. (As of 2024) How do I search for Taekwondo mementos, Dan numbers and certificates? You can check out mementos, Dan numbers, and certificates on the Kukkiwon (World Taekwondo Headquarters) website. [Summary] Korea University is one of best universities in all of Korea. Visitors to Seoul can visit the Korea University Main Hall located in Anam-dong, Seoul.
[Description] Korea University is one of best universities in all of Korea. Visitors to Seoul can visit the Korea University Main Hall located in Anam-dong, Seoul. This beautiful three-story tall building was built in 1932 during the Japanese colonial period. In 1981 the hall was designated Historic Site No. 285 in 1981. The Old Korea University Main Library, located nearby, was designated Historic Site No. 286 in 1981.

[Summary] The National Theater of Korea opened in 1950 and it was the first national, government-supported theater in Asia.
[Description] The National Theater of Korea opened in 1950 and it was the first national, government-supported theater in Asia. There are four theaters where performances take place. The Haeoreum Theater is a large hall, the Daloreum Theater, a small hall, and the Byeoloreum Theater with a stage that is changed according to each performance. The Haneul Theater is a dome-shaped outdoor theater. Performances from a variety of genres including ballet, kabuki, theater, and full pansori take place at the National Theater of Korea.

[Summary] Nakseongdae Park was founded to commemorate General Kang Gam-chan (984-1031), a renowned commander of the Goryeo Dynasty.
[Description] Nakseongdae Park was founded to commemorate General Kang Gam-chan (984-1031), a renowned commander of the Goryeo Dynasty who accomplished a great deal against the Khitan. The name of the site, Nakseongdae, comes from a legend that a large star fell at the moment the general was born. The park features a bronze statue of General Kang Gam-chan on horseback, as well as the Anguksa shrine. The park also forms a dense forest with a variety of trees, such as birch, pine and oak, making it an ideal place to take a stroll.

document_title: Kwanchenru Street: The Little Chinese Quarter of Seoul
document_text:
[Place] Kwanchenru Street: The Little Chinese Quarter of Seoul
[Category] Shopping > Specialty Shops & Stores
[Summary] Unknown to most, this little Chinese quarter in the heart of Seoul is home to some amazing authentic and traditional Chinese restaurants.
[Description] Kwanchenru Street is an unofficial cultural district located in Myeong-dong that is home to incredible Chinese restaurants and stores. Kwanchenru is the Chinese pronunciation of the Korean word "gwancheonga", which means the street in front of a government office. At one of end of Kwanchenru is the Chinese Embassy. Authentic, delicious Chinese food can be had here and there are several famous restaurants here such as Din Tai Fung. There are also several shops selling Chinese antiques, souvenirs, and books. Kwanchenru Street is a well-kept secret for some of the best Chinese restaurants in Seoul.

[Summary] Located in Buam-dong, Changuimun Gate is one of the four minor city gates of Seoul.
[Description] Located in Buam-dong, Changuimun Gate is one of the four minor city gates of Seoul. It is also sometimes referred to as Bukmun (North Gate) or Jahamun. The gate was built by King Taejo, the first king of the Joseon Dynasty, when he constructed the fortifications surrounding the capital. In Korean history, Changuimun Gate is best known by Koreans as the gate that the rebellion faction used to enter Seoul in the Coup of 1623. A road was built to the west of the gate that accommodates traffic but Changuimun Gate itself is closed.

[Place] Bonghwanggak Pavilion
[Category] History > Historical Sites > Others Historical Sites
[Summary] Bonghwanggak Pavilion was constructed in 1912 by Son Byeonghui. In 1969, Bongwhanggak was designated Tangible Cultural Property No. 2 by the Seoul Metropolitan Government
[Description] Bonghwanggak Pavilion was constructed in 1912 by Son Byeonghui, the Korean independence activist. Bongwhanggak was built to be an educational facility that taught students the doctrines of Cheondogyo and educated leaders of the Korean independence movement. Cheondogyo is a Korean religion founded by Choe Je-U and its main tenet is that life and death are one, and all things in the universe repeat in an endless cycle. "Bonghwang" is the Korean word for the phoenix and it appeared often in Choe's writings, which is how the pavilion came to be named Bonghwanggak. The pavilion is considered the main shrine of Cheondogyo. In 1969, Bongwhanggak was designated Tangible Cultural Property No. 2 by the Seoul Metropolitan Government.

document_text:
[Place] Museum of Korea Straw and Plants Handicraft
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Museums
[Summary] A private museum that promotes cultural awareness of straw and its importance as a raw material in Korea since 1992.
[Description] The Museum of Korea Straw and Plants Handicraft is a private museum that was founded in 1992. The museum promotes cultural awareness of straw and its importance as a raw material in Korea. Straw was used in many different ways and is still used today in folk art. The museum's exhibitions display thousands of items made from straw including arts and crafts, tools, relics, and toys. The museum operates various educational programs for laypeople and professionals as well as workshops and crafting classes.

[설명] 대한제국과 일제강점기를 거쳐 명맥이 끊긴 한국 자수를 되살리기 위해 1960 년대 유물을 모아 분석하고 , 한국의 전통 자수 기법을 복원한 흔적을 전부 보존하는 고유의 공간입니다 . 1963 년 문을 연 한국수공예학원이 한상수자수박물관의 시초입니다 . 한국 자수를 보존하고 대중에게 알리기 위해 복합문화공간으로 자리매김하였습니다 . 국가무형문화재 자수장 한상수의 뒤를 이어 장녀가 2 대 관장으로 박물관을 운영하고 있으며 , 3 대 승계를 준비하고 있습니다 . ​

[Place] The Hangsangsoo Embroidery
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Museums
[Summary] A Korean traditional embroidery museum where visitors can discover works of intangible cultural hertiage
[Description] This unique space preserves all the traces of traditional Korean embroidery techniques that have been restored by collecting and analyzing artifacts from the 1960s to revive Korean embroidery, which was lost through the Korean Empire and Japanese occupation. The Korean Handicraft Institute, which opened in 1963, is the origin of the Hansangsu Embroidery Museum. It has been established as a complex cultural space to preserve and present Korean embroidery to the public. The eldest daughter of Han Sang-soo, a National Intangible Cultural Property embroiderer, has been running the museum as the second director and is preparing for the third succession.

document_text:
[Place] Old Seoul Engineering School Main Hall
[Category] History > Historical Sites > Others Historical Sites
[Summary] The Old Seoul Engineering School Main Hall (formerly known as the Central Laboratory Complex) was built in 1906 and designated Historic Site No. 289 in 1981.
[Description] The Old Seoul Engineering School Main Hall (formerly known as the Central Laboratory Complex) was built in 1906 and designated Historic Site No. 289 in 1981. The building was designed by the national Architecture Bureau. While in use as a school, students were taught how to use modern technologies and skills such as dyeing, weaving, papermaking, goldsmithing and woodworking. The building now functions as a museum and is part of Korea National Open University.

[설명] 정릉은 태조의 계비 신덕왕후의 능으로, 극진히 사랑했던 신덕왕후가 갑자기 승하하자 태조는 도성 안 덕수궁 뒤편에 능역을 조성했습니다. 강씨의 봉분 우측에 훗날 자신이 묻힐 자리까지 함께 마련하여 능호를 정릉으로 정하였던 것입니다. 실제로 정릉은 다른 왕릉과 비교했을 때 석물이 빈약합니다. 병풍석이나 난간석은 봉분에서 사라지고 4각 장명등, 고석, 상석 등만이 원래의 것으로 추정됩니다. 장명등의 경우 생김새가 독특한데, 고려 시대 공민왕릉의 양식을 따른 것으로 조선 시대 능역의 가장 오래된 석물인 동시에 예술적 가치가 높습니다. 정릉의 공간은 자연 지형에 맞추어 절선축(折線軸) 기법으로 조성됐습니다. ‘절선축 기법’이란 진입로와 중심 영역의 축이 일직선이 아니라 축을 꺾어서 연결시켜 시각적 흐름을 단절시키는 기법입니다. 걷는 방향에 따라 눈앞에는 새로운 풍경이 펼쳐지고, 이리저리 꺾으면서 거니는 재미가 쏠쏠합니다.

[Place] Jeongneung (A Royal Tomb)
[Category] History > Historical Sites > Tombs & Mausoleums
[Summary] Jeongneung is the royal tomb of Queen Sindeok. She was the second wife of King Taejo, the founder of the Joseon Dynasty.
[Description] Jeongneung is the royal tomb of Queen Sindeok. She was the second wife of King Taejo, the founder of the Joseon Dynasty. It is said that the tomb was originally located behind Deoksugong (Palace) but moved to the current location when a son of King Taejo's first wife, King Taejong ( the third king of the Joseon Dynasty) ascended the throne. The original scale of the tomb was reduced as well. Although it is a simple tomb without many of the stone figures traditionally placed before a royal tomb, it has historical interest as it has faithfully kept the style of an early Joseon period tomb. The tomb is in picturesque surrounds with Bukhansan National Park located nearby .

[설명] 도봉산은 이름 그대로 봉우리가 길인 산입니다. 선인봉을 오르는 암벽 등반 코스만 해도 37개나 됩니다. 매표소 입구를 지나 공원에 들어서면 우암 송시열이 바위에 직접 새긴 글씨가 눈에 띕니다. 도봉산의 입구를 알리는 암각문입니다. 높은 봉우리에 붉은 빛의 구름이 걸린다는 의미의 자운봉은 739.5미터의 도봉산 최고봉입니다. 자운봉 근처에 올라서면 상계동과 의정부가 한눈에 보이고 뒤로는 강화도의 바다가 펼쳐집니다. 웅장한 바위 다섯 개가 나란히 공중에 떠 있는 듯한 오봉은 도봉산 종주 코스에서 빠지지 않습니다. 여기서 마치 소의 양쪽 귀를 닮은 우이암까지 가는 동안 굴곡이 심하지 않은 등산로가 편안하게 이어집니다. 도봉산 자운봉의 동남 방향에 있는 코바위는 도봉산을 가장 아름답게 바라볼 수 있는 최고의 조망지입니다. 풍광이 워낙 아름다워 ‘에덴의 동산’이라고도 부릅니다.

[Place] Dobongsan Mountain
[Category] Nature > Natural Sites(Mountains)
[Summary] Dobongsan Mountain is considered by many to be Seoul’s most dramatic mountain
[Description] Dobongsan Mountain is considered by many to be Seoul’s most dramatic and imposing granite mountain. The mountain's Seoninbong peak is especially popular with rock climbers. Located within Bukhansan National Park, Dobongsan is considered one of Seoul's finest mountains by hiking enthusiasts. The mountain is also surrounded by around 60 temples set in scenic valleys and the temples are great places to see some of Korea's history and culture while enjoying the outdoors.

Munsa-dong is said to be a place where scholars visited their masters to write, serve food, and take refuge in Dobongsan Mountain. [Place] Ichon Hangang Park
[Category] Nature > Natural Sites(Rivers)
[Summary] Features Nodeulseom Island and the northern banks of Hangang River.
[Description] Ichon Hangang Park is made up of Nodeulseom Island and the nearby northern banks of Hangang River. Canola flowers, evening primrose, reeds, cosmos flowers, and other aquatic plants bloom along the banks throughout the season, making it a popular walking trail and cycling spot among locals. Many joggers and inline skaters can also be seen along the trail. Despite its location in the middle of the city, Ichon Hangang Park is a pretty calm and peaceful area where many locals can enjoy recreational sports and activities like soccer, baseball, basketball, volleyball, gateball, tennis, and wood ball. The park also has an inline skating center built in 1998 for international competitions, attracting many inline skaters to enjoy its facilities along the river.

[설명] 대학로의 한국문화예술위원회 건물은 로마네스크 풍의 붉은 석조 건물입니다. 1928년 지어졌으니 80년이 된 건물. 최초의 용도는 경성제국대학의 본관이었습니다. 경성제국대학 본관 건물에는 우리나라 최초의 건축가라고 불리는 박길룡(朴吉龍)도 참여했습니다. 그는 조선총독부 설계에도 참여했으며 화신백화점과 간송미술관 등을 설계했습니다. 경성제국대학 본관은 철근 콘크리트 구조에 벽돌로 벽체를 쌓고 황갈색의 스크래치 타일로 마감했는데 비교적 단순하면서도 견고한 형태입니다. 광복 이후에는 서울대학교 본부로 이용됐습니다. 대학로라는 일대의 지명도 서울대학교에서 기인합니다. 현재는 예술가의 집으로 사용하고 있습니다. 예술가의 집은 우리나라 최초의 대학 본부이자 대학로라는 이름의 근원을 설명하는 유일한 증거기도 합니다. 지난 1981년 사적 제278호로 지정돼 보존해오고 있는 공연,연극 시설입니다.

[요약] 남산공원은 서울에 있는 공원 중에서 가장 넓은 시민공원

[Place] Naksan Park
[Category] Culture > Parks
[Summary] Naksan Park was founded in 2002 to preserve the remaining green spaces after much of the mountain was demolished during the Japanese Occupation.
[Description] Naksan Park was founded in 2002 to preserve the remaining green spaces after much of the mountain was demolished during the Japanese Occupation. There are a range of facilities for visitors including an exhibition hall, a hexagonal pavilion, a senior citizens' center, and sports facilities including badminton and basketball courts and several squares. Despite its modest scale, with a height of just over 100 meters, Naksan was one of the four guardian mountains, along with Bugaksan, Namsan, and Inwangsan, of the capital of the Joseon Dynasty. It took its name from the Korean words, nakta (camel) and san (mountain). In the past, the mountain was popular with yangban, the ruling class of the Joseon Dynasty, who came to see its famous sunset view. In Naksan Park, visitors can follow the walking trail along the Seoul Seonggwak (fortress wall) stretching about 2 km from Hyehwamun to Heunginjimun, the East Gate of Seoul.

[Description] The Maehun Yun Bong-Gil Memorial Hall is dedicated to the resistance fighter, Patriot Yun Bong-gil. Yun's pen name was Maehun and he was active in the Korean independence movement during the Japanese colonial era. Located in Seoul's Yangjae dong, the first floor of the memorial is an exhibition hall that displays relics and biographical information about Yun Bong-gil in chronological order. On the second floor, the exhibition hall contains photographs and other materials of the Korean independence movement organized by theme. Admission to the memorial hall is free.

[Place] Buramsan Mountain
[Category] Nature > Natural Sites(Mountains)
[Summary] Buramsan Mountain is one of Seoul's many beautiful mountains. Buramsan sits between the Nowon-gu neighborhood in Seoul and the city of Namyangju.
[Description] Buramsan Mountain, located across Nowon-gu and Namyangju City, derives its name from a large summit rock resembling a Buddha wearing a peaked hat. It is also known as Cheonbosan Mountain and Pilam Mountain. The mountain features long ridges offering refreshing views. From the summit, you can see Byeollae in Namyangju to the east, Bukhansan and Dobongsan Mountains, Nowon-gu and Dobong-gu to the west, and Namsan Tower and Lotte World Tower to the south. Many visitors come to watch the sunrise. Although the mountain's terrain is relatively simple, it boasts beautiful scenery with its massive rock walls, cliffs, and lush trees. Notable landmarks include Seokjangbong Peak and Turtle Rock. The wooden stairs to the summit make it a relatively easy climb.

[Summary] Haneul Park is the most popular of the five parks situated in World Cup Park which was built to commemorate the 17th FIFA World Cup.
[Description] Haneul Park is one of the five World Cup parks. It was established in 2002 to commemorate the 17th FIFA World Cup by transforming the former Nanjido landfill site. Visitors can enjoy cultural events and programs set against the beautiful backdrop of silver grass fields. [Place] Myeongdong Cathedral
[Category] Culture > Landmarks
[Summary] Myeongdong Cathedral is the very first Roman Catholic parish church in Korea.
[Description] Myeongdong Cathedral is the very first Roman Catholic parish church in Korea. It is also the first Gothic building ever built in Korea and was designated as Historic site No. 285 in Korea. On the basement floor, there is a small sanctuary where the remains of the martyrs are enshrined, and where visitors to the cathedral can pay their respects. Every May, Myeongdong Cathedral holds a cultural festival. The construction of the cathedral started in 1892 and was completed in 1898. Unlike most Gothic buildings, Myeongdong Cathedral was built with bricks instead of stones. It gives the cathedral a characteristic atmosphere. The splendid high ceilings inside the church and the arches in between the magnificent inner pillars show the beautiful Gothic style well. The basement contains the remains of nine saints and martyrs, who devoted their lives to the propagation of Catholicism in Korea. Behind the cathedral, Seongmo Dongsan (St. Mary's garden) is situated. During lunch hour, pipe organs are playing here. The garden offers a peaceful resting space after visiting the cathedral.

[Summary] Tangchundaeseong Fortress was built in 1712 during the Joseon Dynasty to improve the defense of Hanyangdoseong, the Seoul City Wall, and Bukhansanseong Fortress.
[Description] Tangchundaeseong Fortress was built in 1712 during the Joseon Dynasty to improve the defense of Hanyangdoseong, the Seoul City Wall, and the Bukhansanseong Fortress. Hongjimun Gate was built during the reign of King Sukjong, the 19th king of the Joseon Dynasty. Legend has it that King Sukjong wrote “Hongjimun” on the gate's original name-board himself and the gate was called Hongjimun thereafter. [Place] Wongudan Altar
[Category] History > Historical Sites > Modern Architecture
[Summary] Wongudan was built during the Joseon Dynasty to be an altar for performing divine harvest rituals.
[Description] Wongudan was built during the Joseon Dynasty to be an altar for performing divine harvest rituals. Located in central Seoul right near City Hall, it was designated Historic Site No. 157 in 1967. Through the past few centuries the altar was once called Hwandan and more recently Hwangudan. Now officially known as Wongudan Altar, Wongudan is located in close proximity to other major Seoul tourist attractions so it's convenient and easy to add a stop to Wongudan on a Seoul travel itinerary. The current Hwangudan Altar is a complex established in 1897 on the site of the old Nambyeolgung Palace. Its altar was built for Emperor Gojong's enthronement ceremony and rituals. The Japanese demolished the original complex in 1913, and a railway hotel was built on the site, reducing its size. Today, only the Hwangungu, the stone drum, and a stone gate with three arches remain preserved within the grounds of the Joseon Hotel.

[Category] History > Historical Sites > Historical Sites
[Summary] The An Jung-geun Memorial Hall was established to memorialize the Korean patriot An Jung-geun.
[Description] The An Jung-geun Memorial Hall was established to memorialize the Korean patriot An Jung-geun. An fought for Korean independence from Japan and was ultimately executed by Japanese authorities for assassinating Ito Hirobumi in 1909. Ito was a major force behind the Japanese annexation of Korea. The memorial hall is composed of 12 exhibition halls and galleries, an auditorium, a reference library, and a rest area. In addition to exhibition information about An's life and some of his calligraphy, the memorial hall also hosts the An Jung-guen Academny and other events each year. Events include visits to historic sites abroad that were important to independence movements and calligraphy contests. Admission to the An Jung-geun Memorial Hall is free.

[Place] Yeonghwiwon and Sunginwon Royal Tombs
[Category] History > Historical Sites > Tombs & Mausoleums
[Summary] Yeonghwiwon and Sunginwon are the burial site of members of the Korean royal family and the site was designated Historic Site No. 361 in 1991.
[Description] Yeonghwiwon and Sunginwon are the burial site of members of the Korean royal family and the site was designated Historic Site No. 361 in 1991. Yeonghwiwon is the royal tomb of Princess Consort Sunheon, wife of the 26th king of the Joseon Dynasty, Gojong. Sunginwon is the burial place of Crown Prince Yi Jin, grandson of King Gojong and Princess Consort Sunheon. In Korea, tombs for kings and queens are traditionally called “neung” and tombs of princes and royal consorts are called “won”. Yeonghwiwon and Sunginwon were once known as Hongneung as Queen Myeongseong, the first wife of King Gojong was entombed here. The grave was moved to Geumgok-dong in the city of Namyangju in 1919 following the death of King Gojong. Since then, the site has been known as Yeonghwiwon and Sunginwon. Apart from its historic significance, the greenery and beautiful surroundings here have always attracted sightseers.

[Place] Dream Forest
[Category] Nature > Natural Sites(Parks)
[Summary] Dream Forest, located in northern Seoul, is the 4th largest park in the city after Seoul Forest, Olympic Park, and World Cup Park.
[Description] Dream Forest, located in northern Seoul, is the 4th largest park in the city after Seoul Forest, Olympic Park, and World Cup Park. Neighboring six surrounding districts, including Gangbuk-gu, Seongbuk-gu, and Dobong-gu, the park was built on the site where Dreamland amusement park formerly existed. Surrounded by densely forested mountains of Byeogosan Mountain and Opaesan Mountain, Dream Forest provides a variety of attractions to visitors, together with an abundant amount of natural vegetation. The Cherry Blossom Path in the spring or the Maple Tree Forest in the fall are especially beautiful. Visitors will also find attractions designed after traditional Korean architecture such as the Wolyeongji (Moon Reflecting Pond) and the Wolgwang Falls (Moonlight Falls). At the top of the observatory, visitors are treated to a panoramic view of the whole park and a view of Bukhansan Mountain, Dobongsan Mountain and Suraksan Mountain. Dream Forest also accommodates various cultural venues. The Dream Forest Arts Center, with its Performance Hall and Concert Hall, the Sangsang Toktok Art Museum and several grassy lawns and plazas offer concerts and performances throughout the year. Several restaurants and cafes are also conveniently located within the park, making Dream Forest one of the most comprehensive parks in Seoul.

[Place] Korea Central Mosque
[Category] History > Religious Sites
[Summary] The Seoul Central Mosque was established to be a place to worship for Muslims in Korea as well as to educate the larger public about Islam and Islamic cultures.
[Description] Located in Hannam-dong, Yongsan-gu, Seoul, the Seoul Central Mosque is the first Islamic Mosque in Korea. It was established on May 21, 1976, after construction began in October 1974. The Korean government provided the site in May 1969 with approximately 4,958 square meters of land, and the construction costs were supported by Islamic countries worldwide, including Saudi Arabia. Situated between the Hangang River and Namsan Mountain, the mosque features prayer halls on the first and second floors, with ablution rooms for men and women in the basement of the annex building. The first floor of the annex houses classrooms, while the second floor has office spaces. The adjacent Islamic Center includes facilities such as an Islamic mission center for children, a Muslim congregation, a women's association, and a library. The exterior of the Seoul Central Mosque features a variety of amenities, including halal restaurants, a halal butcher shop, an Islamic bookstore, a halal supermarket, and a travel agency, making it convenient for Muslims and non-Muslims to visit. [Place] Seoul Art Space - Sindang Creative Arcade
[Category] Culture > Cultural Districts
[Summary] The Sindang Creative Arcade is a creative space for artists and an art market.
[Description] The Sindang Creative Arcade is a creative space for artists and an art market. The arcade was re-born into a space for the arts following renovation of empty storefronts at the Sindang Underground Shopping Center in the Jungang Market. The Jungang Market was established in 1917 and the renovation that created the Sindang Creative Arcade has revitalized the area. The creative arcade houses workshops and an art market. Dozens of artists create artworks and crafts in nearly every art medium there is. At the art market, shoppers can purchase unique artwork and items.

[요약] 한국 최초로 세워진 난타 전용극장
[설명] 홍대난타극장은 한국 최초로 세워진 전용극장입니다. 난타전용관에서 공연하는 ‘난타’는 한국의 전통 가락인 사물놀이 리듬을 바탕으로 하여 주방에서 일어나는 일들을 코믹하게 드라마화한 비언어극입니다. 한국의 대표적인 창작 공연물인 난타는 영국 에딘버러 프린지 페스티벌 전석매진, 한국 최초 브로드웨이 장기공연 이라는 신기록을 세운 공연입니다. 난타전용관은 ‘난타’만을 공연하기 위해 꾸며져 극의 재미와 효과를 극대한 조명과 무대 세트로 꾸며져 있습니다. 연간 38만명의외국 관광객이 난타공연장을 찾습니다. 난타는 비언어극이기 때문에 국적을 불문하고 큰 호응을 얻었습니다. ‘홍대난타극장’에서는 매일 난타 공연이 열립니다. 주방의 모든 것을 활용한 타악 연주 사이사이 한국의 전통 춤과 관객 참여가 어우러져 흥겨운 축제 한 마당이 벌어집니다.

[Summary] Nanta Theater is Korea’s first exclusive venue for Nanta performances, which are based on the rhythm of the samulnori (traditional Korean percussion quartet) and are comic non-verbal plays set in a kitchen.
[Description] Nanta Theater is Korea’s first exclusive venue for Nanta performances, which are based on the rhythm of the samulnori (traditional Korean percussion quartet) and are comic non-verbal plays set in a kitchen. Nanta has been a sell-out success at the Edinburgh Fringe Festival in the UK and was also the first long-running Korean show on Broadway in New York City. The shows have been so successful that they now run at three exclusive theaters in Seoul which are equipped with special lighting and sound systems to create maximum audience impact. Around 380,000 international tourists visit Nanta Theater every year.

[Description] Uireung is the royal tomb of King Gyeongjong, the 20th king of the Joseon dynasty, and his wife Queen Seonui. Uireung is located inside the Korea National University of Arts campus in Seokgwan-dong, Seongbuk-gu. Most royal tombs are "ssangneung," tombs that are arranged with the king and queen next to each other. At Uireung, the tombs of the king and the queen are arranged front to back. The tomb in the front is Queen Seonui’s and the one in the back belongs to King Gyeongjong. Uireung is closed Mondays.

[Category] History > Historical Sites > Tombs & Mausoleums
[Summary] Heonilleung is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the final resting place of two pairs of the Joseon Dynasty's kings and queens.
[Description] Heonilleung is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the final resting place of two pairs of the Joseon Dynasty's kings and queens. The name of the site is a combination of the names of the two separate tombs, Heonleung and Inleung. The tombs of Joseon's third king, Taejong (1367-1422), and his wife, Queen Wongyeong (1365-1420) are at Heonleung. Inleung is the resting place of Joseon's 23rd king, Sunjo (1790-1834), and his wife Queen Sunwon (1789-1857). Heonilleung is unique in that it houses two kings born 400 years apart. Visitors to the royal tombs can see examples of early and late Joseon Dynasty royal tombs and there is a weekly talk about the tombs every Saturday. On Lunar New Year's Day, traditional performances are held at Heonilleung for the public to enjoy.

[Description] The Seoul Olympic Museum was established to commemorate the 1988 Olympics in Seoul and to promote the Olympic spirit. Located within Olympic Park, the museum is multipurpose space that is a combination of a park and sports scenter. Visitors can take part in activities and education programs. There is also a cafeteria on the second floor and a museum shop for souvenirs. Admission to the Seoul Olympic Museum is free.

[Summary] Cheongwadae, also known as the Blue House, is the Korean presidential residence.
[Description] Cheong Wa Dae, meaning "Blue House," was the official residence of the President of South Korea until it was opened to the public in June 2022, becoming a popular tourist destination. The main building features the president's office, reception rooms, and conference rooms, while auxiliary buildings include Chunchugwan, the State Guest House, and the rear garden. Cheong Wa Dae is closed every Tuesday, and tour reservations can be made on its official website. A tour of the Cheong Wa Dae grounds, which encompasses Nokjiwon, Sangchunjae, the residence, the State Guest House, and the main building, typically takes around 1 hour and 30 minutes to 2 hours. On rainy days, interior tours of key buildings like the main building and Chunchugwan may be restricted to prevent damage. In the event of natural disasters such as typhoons, tours of all or parts of Cheong Wa Dae may be suspended to ensure visitor safety.

[요약] 한국 최초로 세워진 난타전용극장.
[설명] 난타전용관은 한국 최초로 세워진 전용극장입니다. 난타전용관에서 공연하는 ‘난타’는 한국의 전통 가락인 사물놀이 리듬을 바탕으로 하여 주방에서 일어나는 일들을 코믹하게 드라마화한 비언어극입니다. 한국의 대표적인 창작 공연물인 난타는 영국 에딘버러 프린지 페스티벌 전석매진, 한국 최초 브로드웨이 장기공연 이라는 신기록을 세운 공연입니다. 난타전용관은 ‘난타’만을 공연하기 위해 꾸며져 극의 재미와 효과를 극대한 조명과 무대 세트로 꾸며져 있습니다. 연간 38만명의외국 관광객이 난타공연장을 찾습니다. 난타는 비언어극이기 때문에 국적을 불문하고 큰 호응을 얻었습니다. ‘명동난타극장’에서는 매일 난타 공연이 열립니다. 주방의 모든 것을 활용한 타악 연주 사이사이 한국의 전통 춤과 관객 참여가 어우러져 흥겨운 축제 한 마당이 벌어집니다.

[Place] Jong Ie Nara Paper Art Museum
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Art Museums/Galleries
[Summary] Jong Ie Nara Paper Art Museum educates the public on the history and development of paper in Korea through fun activities programs and museum displays.
[Description] The Jongienara Museum opened in 1999 as a Paper Art Museum and was established to revive and recreate Korea's world-class paper, K origami, and paper culture. Reopened as the Jongienara Museum in 2008, it goes beyond researching and introducing Korea's outstanding origami and paper culture. It pays attention to the excellent role of paper as a craft and art object, presenting the development of a new cultural art genre and modern paper culture and art. The excellence and creativity of Korean origami and paper culture are known to the public through the discovery, exhibitions, and education of current cultural paper artworks.

[Summary] Korea’s presidential residence, Cheogwadae, has a newly-renovated “Sarangchae,” or a front-most section.
[Description] Cheongwadae Sarangchae is a historical memorial museum where visitors can learn about the past, present, and future visions of Seoul and Korea. Originally the home of the public information hall of Cheongwadae (the Blue House, the Korean presidential residence) called “Hyojadong Sarangbang”, it re-opened with its present name in January 2010 after extensive renovation. Cheongwadae Sarangchae is a two-story building, with exhibition halls, souvenir shops, a resting area on the first floor, and experience zones on the second floor. Cheongwadae Sarangchae features the Korea Hall, the Hi Seoul Hall, a traditional handicrafts demonstration room, a souvenir shop, and a café on the first floor. Various cultural events, such as demonstrations of traditional handicrafts and traditional Korean tea tasting, are held regularly in the lobby. The souvenir shop stocks Cheongwadae-themed goods and traditional Korean items. After viewing the exhibitions, it is pleasant to take a break at the café and enjoy a cup of traditional Korean tea. The Presidential Hall on the second floor displays material about the former presidents of Korea. Here visitors can explore the political and economic events of Korea from the past up to the present day via pictures and visuals. Visitors can also see at a glance a chronology of the past 60 years of Korean history, as well as the major events in the democratization and industrialization of Korea.

[Category] History > Religious Sites
[Summary] Jinkwansa Temple, located in Bukhansan National Park, is a temple established by the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. Jinkwansa offers temple stays.
[Description] Jinkwansa Temple is a centuries-old temple located in Bukhansan National Park. The temple was built by order of King Hyeonjong of the Goryeo Dynasty in gratitude to the great Buddhist priest Jinkwan. History has it that Jinkwan saved King Hyeon-jong's life when he was young and the king repaid the priest by building the temple. Jinkwansa Temple is comprised of several buildings and some of the notable buildings include Daeungjeon Hall, Myeongbujeon Hall, and Nahanjeon Hall. The temple also operates temple stay programs where visitors can experience Buddhist culture firsthand. There are programs for groups, children, and youths.

[Summary] Learn about the history of education in Korea at the Appenzeller Noble Memorial Museum.
[Description] Learn about the history of education in Korea at the Appenzeller Noble Memorial Museum. The museum is housed in what was once the Pai Chai Hakdang, which was Korea's first Western-style school. Currently, the school's classrooms have been repurposed and are used as a permanent exhibition hall, a special exhibition hall, an experience zone, and a seminar room. In the permanent exhibition hall, visitors can see what the Pai Chai Hakdang looked like in the 1930s at the hall's recreated historical classroom. Admission to the museum is free.

document_title: National Museum of Korean Contemporary History
document_text:
[Place] National Museum of Korean Contemporary History
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Museums
[Summary] The National Museum of Korean Contemporary History houses exhibitions that spans modern Korean history, from the 19th century to today.
[Description] The National Museum of Korean Contemporary History houses exhibitions that span modern Korean history, from the first opening of Korea to outsiders in the late 19th century to today. The museum is the country's first national museum of contemporary history. The eight-story museum has many facilities: there are four permanent exhibition halls and two special exhibition halls, seminar rooms, lecture halls, a rooftop garden, a museum shop (that sells souvenirs), a cafe, and storage lockers. The four permanent exhibitions cover different periods of Korean history and there are over 1,500 artifacts and items here. Some of the displays are patriot Ahn Jung-Geun's last writings, the March 1st Declaration of Independence, belongings of fallen soldiers from the Korean War, and materials relating to democratic activism. The museum's first floor contains two special exhibition halls. Here, you will find a variety of limited-time exhibitions relating to Korean history, politics, society, and culture. Additionally, visitors can listen to, watch, and experience the modernization of Korea through state-of-the-art technology. There is also the Children's Museum, where children can learn and experience history for themselves with the museum’s “Our History’s Treasure Chest” area.

document_title: Kyung Hee University Natural History Museum
document_text:
[Place] Kyung Hee University Natural History Museum
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Museums
[Summary] Founded in 1978, the Kyunghee University Natural History Museum is run by the university.
[Description] Upon opening its doors in 1978, the Kyunghee University Natural History Museum served as a little respite of nature in the city that boasted of a collection of nearly 90,000 specimen on display. The museum was initially founded upon the purpose of realizing the Kyungee University founding ideology of "Creating a world of culture" grounded in the results that had been obtained through several years of studying nature. The effort continues to approach the distancing relationship between nature and humankind amid rapid societal changes and urbanization with a "respite of nature in the city" that provides a sense of living in harmony with nature. All six floors of the museum display easy-to-understand exhibits capturing a comparison between the current state of evolution and the process of transformation up to the present-day with specimen of different plants and animals, as well as various rocks from sedimentary to igneous and metamorphic rocks that were used for research purposes by specialized teams of professors in various fields. There are courses and tour programs offered to help understand and practice nature preservation and the importance of life within the framework of these exhibited specimen.

[Place] Son Kee Chung Memorial Hall
[Category] History > Historical Sites > Others Historical Sites
[Summary] The Son Kee Chung Memorial Hall honors the athlete and gold medalist, Son Kee Chung.
[Description] The Son Kee Chung Memorial Hall honors the athlete and gold medalist, Son Kee Chung. The memorial hall opened on October 14th, 2012, marking the centennial anniversary of Son's birth. The memorial hall was once a school and was in fact Son's alma mater. Son Kee Chung was a gold medalist in the 1936 Berlin Olympics Marathon. Though Son Kee Chung was registered as a Japanese athlete, due to the Japanese occupation of the Korean peninsula, his victory was cherished and praised by Korean nationals. Visit the memorial hall to learn more about Son's life and how he won his gold medal. Admission is free and there are sometimes special exhibitions.

[요약] 매년 봄, 가을 화려한 궁중 문화 체험고종·명성황후 가례 재현 행사
[설명] 고종·명성후 가례는 고종 즉위 3년(1866년)되는 해에 왕비로 책봉된 명성후(明成后) 민씨가 별궁인 운현궁 노락당(老樂堂)에 거처하면서 궁중 예법과 가례 절차를 교육받고, 그해 음력 3월 21일 거행된 15세의 고종과 16세의 명성후 민씨의 국혼례를 재현하는 행사입니다. 고종·명성후 가례 재현은 왕비로 책봉된 명성후가 책봉 교명을 받는 ‘비수책(妃受冊)’ 의식으로 시작된다. 한편 비수책 중에 고종이 왕의 가마인 어연(御輦)을 타고 많은 호위 관원 및 군사들과 함께 운현궁으로 행차하는 ‘어가행렬(御駕行列)’이 진행됩니다. 임금이 운현궁에 들어서면, 예비 왕비의 거처인 별궁에 친히 거동하여 명성후를 맞이하는 ‘친영(親迎) 의식’이 재현됩니다. 가례의 시작과 중간에 운현궁에서만 볼 수 있는 다양한 궁중무용 행사가 펼쳐집니다. 궁중에서 경사스런 잔치에 연행되었던 무애무(無?舞), 검무(劍舞), 무고(舞鼓), 보상무(寶相舞) 등 품격 높은 ‘궁중정재(宮中呈才)’가 공연됩니다. 또한 가례 재현 행사 후에는 운현궁을 찾은 관람객을 위해 배우들과 함께 무대 앞에서 기념촬영을 할 수 있는 시간도 마련됩니다.

[설명] 남산에 오르면 눈길을 끄는 검은 벽돌의 굴뚝 다섯 개가 있습니다. 서울특별시 기념물 제14호 남산봉수대입니다. 서울시의 전경을 조망하기에도 좋지만 예전에는 릴레이식 통신 수단의 일종이었습니다. 변방의 급박한 사정이나 위급한 사태를 신속히 전달하기 위해 전국 각지에 설치하고 봉수를 올려 중앙으로 소식을 전했습니다. 남산봉수대의 역사는 조선 개국 초기로 거슬러 올라갑니다. 태조는 1394년 한양에 수도를 정하고 남산에 봉수대를 설치했습니다. 전국의 봉수에서 올라오는 소식이 최종적으로 전해지는 중앙 봉수소였습니다. 남산의 옛이름을 따 목멱산(木覓山) 봉수라고도 하고 서울의 의미를 따 경봉수라고도 했습니다. 다섯 개의 봉수대에 낮에는 연기, 밤에는 불을 피워 신호했는데 그 수에 따라 의미가 달라졌습니다. 평상(평화) 시에는 하나, 적이 나타나면 둘, 경계에 접근하면 셋, 침범하면 넷, 적과 아군이 충돌하면 다섯을 피워 올렸습니다. 조선 시대 때는 전국적으로 673개의 봉수가 있었는데 어떤 일이 생겨도 하루 만에 서울의 남산봉수대까지 소식이 전해졌다고 합니다. 남산에는 원래 각기 다른 다섯 군데에 봉수대가 있었는데 팔각정 앞의 남산봉수대는 그 가운데 하나를 1993년 복원한 것입니다. 남산봉수대는 갑오개혁 다음 해인 1895년까지 불이나 연기를 피워 올렸습니다. 이후 1993년‘청구도’등 관련 자료를 종합해 복원했으나 낙서 등 훼손이 심해 2005년부터 출입을 폐쇄했습니다. 그러다 2007년 다시 개방하며 거화의식도 함께 진행하고 있습니다. 거화의식은 월요일을 제외한 매일 정오를 전후해 열립니다. 의식은 정오 약 30분 전부터 봉수대를 지키는 수위의식과 봉수대 주변을 순찰하는 순라의식을 시작으로 진행됩니다. 정오가 가까워지면 봉수군들의 나발과 나각 소리가 거화의식이 곧 진행될 것임을 알립니다. 종로의 종각에서 12번의 타종이 울리면 그때 비로소 연기를 피워 올립니다. 큰일이 없는 평상 시이므로 앞서 말한 거화의 원칙에 따라 하나의 봉화만을 올립니다. 거화의식이 전체 의식의 하이라이트긴 하지만 이를 전후에 펼쳐지는 수위의식과 순라의식 역시 주목할 만합니다. 덕수궁 왕궁수문장 교대의식에 비해 규모는 작지만 봉화라는 지리적 특징이 더해져 색다른 볼거리를 제공합니다. 거화의식이 완전히 끝난 후에는 봉수군과 기념촬영도 할 수 있습니다.

[Place] Namsan Beacon Mound Lighting Ceremony
[Category] Festivals/Events/Performances
[Summary] The Namsan Beacon Mound Lighting Ceremony is a re-enactment of Bongsu, a communication system that was once used to notify the government of urgent military matters occurring at the city borders. After being reconstructed in 2007, a re-enactment of how the Beacon Mound was used during the Joseon Dynasty has been held from 11:30 to 12:30 daily (except Mondays).
[Description] The Namsan Beacon Mound Lighting Ceremony is a re-enactment of Bongsu, a communication system that was used to notify the central government of urgent military matters (e.g. the approach of enemy forces, etc.) from the borders during ancient times. Bongsu was used to send messages across the peninsula by using smoke during the daytime and torchlights at night, a more convenient and rapid messaging method than horse or messenger. "Bongsu" is a combination of the words "bong" meaning torchlight, and "su" meaning smoke. Namsan Beacon Mound was established after moving the capital city to Hanyang (present day Seoul) during the third year of King Taejo's reign (1394) during the Joseon Dynasty period. To protect the city from invasions, castle walls were built on the four major mountains located within the city: Bugaksan, Inwangsan, Naksan, and Namsan. On Namsan, five beacons were built at its peak to report political and military information to the king.

[Place] Namsan Beacon Mound Lighting Ceremony
[Primary category] Festivals/Events/Performances

on the four major mountains located within the city: Bugaksan, Inwangsan, Naksan, and Namsan. On Namsan, five beacons were built at its peak to report political and military information to the king. One beacon was lit at normal times, two when an enemy appeared, three when an enemy approached the border, four when an enemy invaded the border and five beacons were lit when a battle with an enemy had begun at the border. Namsan Beacon Mound served as the central destination point for all beacons in the peninsula because of its proximity to the King. At the peak of the Chosun dynasty, 673 beacon towers transmitted military and political information from around the peninsula to the capital Seoul. Historical records state that it took 12 hours for a message to travel from Busan to Seoul, two cities approximately 500 kilometers apart. Namsan Beacon Mound was used for approximately 500 years until 1894, the year after Gabo Reformation. Namsan Beacon Mound was also called "Mokmyeoksan Beacon Mound" as Namsan was once called Mokmyeoksan, and was even called "Gyeong Beacon Mound" as it was located in Seoul. Originally there were five different beacon mound stations located on Namsan, but they were destroyed over the course of time. The current beacon mound was reconstructed in 1993 based on historical records in one of the five locations, near Namsan Palgakjeong Pavilion), and has been designated Seoul Monument No. 14. Starting from 2007, a re-enactment of how the Beacon Mound was used during the Joseon Dynasty has been held from 11:30 to 12:30 every day except on Mondays.

[Place] Namsan Beacon Mound Lighting Ceremony
[Primary category] Festivals/Events/Performances

has been designated Seoul Monument No. 14. Starting from 2007, a re-enactment of how the Beacon Mound was used during the Joseon Dynasty has been held from 11:30 to 12:30 every day except on Mondays. The event starts with a patrolling ceremony and a ceremony of the guards. At around noon, the bongsugun (beacon tower soldiers) sound the bugle and conch horn to signify that the lighting ceremony is about to begin. Then at exactly noon, Bosingak Belfry located in Jongno rings twelve times, and the lighting ceremony begins. Only one beacon is lit in accordance with the rules that were used in ancient times. Although the lighting ceremony itself is great to see, the patrolling ceremony and ceremony of the guards that occurs before and after the lighting ceremony are very interesting to see as well. Although smaller in size than the Changing of the Guards ceremony that takes place at Deoksugung Palace, these ceremonies offer the opportunity to witness a different aspect of traditional Korean culture. Once the event has concluded, visitors may take photos with the bongsugun.

document_title: Changing of the Royal Guard at Gyeongbokgung Palace
document_text:
[Place] Changing of the Royal Guard at Gyeongbokgung Palace
[Category] Festivals/Events/Performances
[Summary] A must-see among Seoul's tourist attractions, this ceremony is a great opportunity to experience a rare traditional scene in Korea, as the ceremony is reenacted exactly as it used to be held, with guards wearing royal uniforms, carrying traditional weapons and playing traditional instruments.
[Description] During the Joseon Dynasty, the royal guards were responsible for guarding and patrolling the gates of the capital city and the royal palaces. The royal palace guards, who were known as the "Wanggung Sumunjang", had the very important duty of protecting theking by guarding the entrance gates of the primary royal palace where the king resided. They were in charge of opening and closing the palace gates, inspecting all visitors, and maintaining a close surveillance of the palace. They were divided intodayand night shifts, and the Changing of the Guard ceremony took place whenever the shifts changed over. In the early period of the Joseon Dynasty, the Changing of the Guard ceremony was conducted at Gyeongbokgung Palace as at that time Gyeongbokgung was the primary royal palace and the king then resided there. However, in the late period of the Joseon DynastywhenGyeongbokgung was burned down during the Imjin Waeran (Japanese Invasions of 1592 - 1598), Deoksugung was made the primary royal palace and the Changing of the Guard ceremony was then conducted at Deoksugung.

was burned down during the Imjin Waeran (Japanese Invasions of 1592 - 1598), Deoksugung was made the primary royal palace and the Changing of the Guard ceremony was then conducted at Deoksugung. After some extensive historical research, this splendid and elegant traditional Korean royal court cultural ceremony was first re-enacted in 1996 and has been a must-see among Seoul's tourist attractions ever since. This ceremony is a great opportunity to experiencea rare traditional scene in Korea, as the ceremony is reenacted exactly as it used to be held, with guards wearing royal uniforms, carrying traditional weapons and playing traditional instruments. A tradition comparable to the Changing of the Guards atBuckingham Palace, this ceremony takes place twice a day in front of Gwanghwamun, the main gate of Gyeongbokgung at 10 a.m. and 2 p.m. (except on Tuesdays).

[요약] 2014년 1월부터 매월 마지막 수요일이 ‘문화가 있는 날’로 정해졌다. 문화가 있는 날에는 관람료 무료•할인 혜택이 제공되고, 야간개방 및 문화프로그램 등이 확대 시행된다.
[설명] 2014년 1월부터 매월 마지막 수요일이 ‘문화가 있는 날’로 정해졌다. 문화가 있는 날에는 관람료 무료•할인 혜택이 제공되고, 야간개방 및 문화프로그램 등이 확대 시행된다. ‘문화가 있는 날’에는 유료로 운영 중이던 국•공•사립 전시 관람시설은 물론, 많은 국민이 즐기는 영화, 프로스포츠와 관람료가 다소 부담이 되던 공연프로그램도 대폭 할인된 가격에 즐길 수 있다. 또한, 국공립 박물관•미술관, 도서관은 야간개방도 실시한다.

[장소명] The GREAT Festival(영국 문화 축제)
[카테고리] 축제/공연/행사 > 축제
[요약] 주한영국대사관은 영국 국가 홍보 ‘GREAT 캠페인’의 일환으로 2014년 3월 27일부터 31일까지 5일간 신사동 가로수길에서 <2014 The GREAT Festival(영국 문화 축제)>을 진행한다.
[설명] 주한영국대사관은 영국 국가 홍보 ‘GREAT 캠페인’의 일환으로 2014년 3월 27일부터 31일까지 5일간 신사동 가로수길에서 <2014 The GREAT Festival(영국 문화 축제)>을 진행한다. 올해 국내에서 열리는 은 영국 주력 산업 분야인 패션, 디자인, 음식 및 주류의 우수성을 알리고자 ‘Fashion is GREAT’, ‘Creativity is GREAT’, ‘Food is GREAT’, ‘Pubs are GREAT’ 등의 주제 하에 다채로운 이벤트를 선보인다. 올 봄 서울의 가장 트렌디한 장소인 가로수길에 입점된 개성 넘치는 영국 브랜드숍의 특별 프로모션과 이벤트는 물론, 다양한 영국의 펍 문화와 음식 문화를 체험해 볼 수 있다. 이번 페스티벌에서는 신사의 나라 또는 영국 왕실등에서 비롯된 영국의 고전적인 기존 이미지를 벗은 현대적이면서 감각적인 영국 브랜드와 문화 콘텐츠를 한 곳에서 체험할 수 있게 될 것이다. 2월 마지막 주부터 페스티벌 기간(4월 첫째 주)까지 주한영국대사관 페이스북에서는 GREAT 캠페인과 페스티벌에 대한 자세한 소개 및 다양한 퀴즈, 경품 이벤트를 진행한다. GREAT 캠페인은 영국의 다채로운 문화와 산업을 홍보하고, 비즈니스 파트너로서의 영국의 이미지를 제고하며, 국제적인 관심을 도모하기 위해 3년째 진행되고 있다.
[주소] 서울특별시 강남구 신사동

[장소명] 도성길라잡이와 함께하는 한양도성투어
[카테고리] 축제/공연/행사 > 축제
[요약] 한양도성 무료 해설 투어「도성길라잡이와 함께하는 한양도성투어」프로그램이 3월부터 12월까지 매주 일요일(13:30∼17:00)에 진행된다. 해설은 한양도성 안내해설자원활동가인 ‘서울KYC 도성길라잡이’ 가 무료로 진행하며, 4개 코스를 주별로 돌아가면서 진행한다.
[설명] 한양도성 무료 해설 투어「도성길라잡이와 함께하는 한양도성투어」프로그램이 3월부터 12월까지 매주 일요일(13:30∼17:00)에 진행된다. 해설은 한양도성 안내해설자원활동가인 ‘서울KYC 도성길라잡이’ 가 무료로 진행하며, 4개 코스를 주별로 돌아가면서 진행한다. 4개 투어코스는 ▴1주차 ‘광희문〜숭례문’ ▴2주차 ‘숭례문〜창의문’ ▴3주차 ‘창의문〜혜화문’ ▴4주차 ‘혜화문〜광희문’으로, 소요시간은 약 3시간 30분 정도(13:30〜17:00) 소요된다. 해설이 함께하는 이번 투어의 매력은 내사산 숲길과 도심, 주택가에 남아있는 한양도성의 흔적을 만나는 데 있다. 4개 구간별로 펼쳐지는 다양한 풍경과 이야기는 600년 성곽도시 수도 서울에서만 느낄 수 있는 특별한 도보여행인 셈이다. 몸과 마음이 바쁜 도시민에게 18.6km의 한양도성 걷기는 작은 쉼과 휴식의 시간을 제공해 줄 것이다.
[태그] 해설, 한양도성, 도성길라잡이, 무료해설투어, 서울KYC도성길라잡이
[이용 시간] 2014년 3~12월 매주 일요일, 13:30〜17:00(약 3시간 30분 소요)
[참고 사항] <투어코스 소개>

1주차 : (광희문∼숭례문) 구간은 태조, 세종시대의 축성방법과 공사책임제를 보여주는 각자성석을 만날 수 있다. 

2주차 : (숭례문∼창의문) 구간은 5년 동안의 복구공사를 마친 숭례문의 모습과 서울의 자연경관적 가치를 한 눈에 조망할 수 있는 인왕산코스로 구성되어 있다. 

3주차 : (창의문∼혜화문) 구간은 출입이 제한된 곳으로, 참석시 반드시 신분증을 지참해야만 참여할 수 있다. 이 구간에서의 추천 조망점은 청운마루로 경복궁과 광화문으로 이어지는 조선시대 도시 설계의 핵심을 만날 수 있다.
 
4주차 : (혜화문∼광희문) 구간은 어린이와 노약자가 쉽게 참여할 수 있는 구간으로 특히, 혜화문에서 낙산공원의 탐방로가 잘 조성되어 있다. 도성 인근마을인 이화동 벽화마을과 장수마을을 함께 만날 수 있는 점도 이 구간의 매력이다.

[장소명] 꽃피는 3월, 서울시 문화예술 프로그램 안내
[카테고리] 축제/공연/행사 > 축제
[요약] 꽁꽁 언 겨울을 지나 꽃피는 봄, 3월이 돌아왔다. 새봄을 기다렸다 활짝 피어나는 꽃망울처럼 서울의 문화예술프로그램이 쏟아진다.
[설명] 세계인이 가장 좋아하는 화가인 빈센트 반 고흐를 재조명한 뮤지컬, <빈센트 반 고흐> 가 4월 27일까지 충무아트홀에서 펼쳐진다. ‘별이 빛나는 밤에’, ‘해바라기’ 등 고흐의 살아 숨 쉬는 그림을 3D 프로젝션 맵핑 기법을 활용해 무대 위에 펼치고, 그의 인생을 담은 음악과 함께 선보인다. 서울시립교향악단은 3월 21일 세종문화회관 체임버홀에서 <실내악 시리즈> 의 두 번째 무대로 다양한 편성의 윈드 앙상블 작품을 선보인다. 이번 무대에서 연주하는 모차르트 <세레나데 10번> ‘그랑파르티타’는 13개의 관악기와 7악장으로 구성된 대규모 실내악 작품으로 치밀하고 탄탄한 구조 속에서 다채로운 관악기의 매력을 느낄 수 있는 작품이다. <내 마음의 슈퍼맨> 은 평범하지만 위대한 영웅인 아버지에 대해서 진지하게 생각해보게 하는 작품으로 각박한 사회를 살아가는 우리들의 마음속에 뜨거운 감동을 불러일으킬 국내 초연인 연극이다. 충무아트홀에서 3월 8일부터 만날 수 있다. 노원문화예술회관에서는 3월 29일 코미디 뮤지컬 <넌센스> 가 펼쳐진다. 뮤지컬 <넌센스>는 1991년 국내 초연 이후 23년 동안 최장공연기록과 최다관객기록을 세운 최고의 히트작이다.
[태그] 축제, 행사, 3월 문화행사, 서울시 행사

[장소명] 한강 역사탐방 프로그램「한강의 역사를 찾아서」

[설명] 서울시는 우리 민족의 젖줄인 한강의 역사를 시민들에게 알리기 위해 한강과 그 주변 역사문화유적지를 연계한 한강 역사 여행 10대 탐방코스를 4월 1일(화)부터~11월 29일(토)까지 운영한다. 「한강의 역사를 찾아서」는 ▲ ‘도보코스’ ▲ ‘선상코스’와 ▲ 한강역사해설사가 학교 또는 지자체에서 운영하는 단체 등에 직접 찾아가서 한강 관련 역사, 문화 및 인물에 관해 역사해설을 해주는 ‘찾아가는 역사탐방’ 등 세 개 코스로 운영된다. 프로그램 성격에 따라 개인 또는 단체 접수로 나뉘며, 예약접수는 3월 17일(월)부터 시작해 운영기간 내(4월 1일~11월 29일) 언제라도 신청이 가능하다. 개인신청은 ‘도보코스’(1코스 광나루길~9코스 겸재정선길)만 가능하며, ‘찾아가는 역사 탐방’ 프로그램은 학교를 포함한 단체 신청, ‘선상코스(한강 옛 나루터길)’는 학교만 신청이 가능하다. 10개 코스의 평균 소요시간은 1시간~2시간 30분(선택사항)이다. ‘도보코스’와 ‘찾아가는 역사 탐방’ 프로그램 참가를 원하는 시민들은 서울시공공서비스예약시스템( http://yeyak.seoul.go.kr )을 통해 참여희망일 10일전까지 신청하면 된다. ‘도보코스’는 월~토요일 오전 10시~오후 4시까지 진행되며, 1회 팀당 3~40명까지 가능하다. (3명 미만일 경우 프로그램이 취소됨) ‘찾아가는 역사 탐방’ 프로그램은 월~금요일 오전 10시~오후 4시까지 진행되며, 학교 또는 노인대학 등 지자체에서 운영하는 단체 교육 프로그램을 대상으로 한다. (인원수 제한 없음) ‘선상코스(한강 옛 나루터길)’는 주 5일제 수업과 관련해 특별 기획한 청소년을 위한 프로그램으로(초·중·고등학교에서만 신청가능), 개인 신청은 불가하다. 매주 토요일 오전 10~12시까지 운영하며, 최소인원은 15명이고 최대 50명까지 가능하다.(방학기간에는 운영하지 않음) 프로그램에 참여하고 싶은 사람들은 21일전까지 한강사업본부 수상관리과로 전화신청(☎02-3780-0825)하면 된다. 전체 프로그램 관련 자세한 내용은 한강사업본부 문화홍보과(☎02-3780-0762)로 문의하면 된다.

[Description] The Gwanghwamun International Art Festival (GIAF) is an annual art festival that aims to improve the quality of Korean art and pop culture. [장소명] 덕수궁 왕궁수문장 교대의식
[카테고리] 축제/공연/행사 > 축제
[요약] 왕궁수문장 교대의식은 조선시대 왕궁에는 수문군이라는 군대가 있어 궁궐 문을 개폐, 경비, 순찰하는 업무 등을 수행하였다. 왕궁 수문장 교대의식은 영국 왕실의 근위병 교대의식과 비견되는 화려하고 품위 있는 한국전통 궁중 문화 재현행사이다.
[설명] 교대를 앞둔 두 무리의 수문군이 대한문 앞에서 마주한다. 카메라나 캠코더로 장면을 담기에 여념이 없는 외국인 관광객도 많다. 북소리가 울리기 전부터 덕수궁 대한문 앞 광장은 왕궁수문장 교대의식을 보기 위해 모여든 사람으로 가득하다. 수문군을 빙 둘러 포위한 형세다. 엄고수(북을 치는 이)의 힘찬 손동작이 허공을 가른다. 둥! 둥! 둥! 세 번의 북소리. 수문장 교대의식을 알리는 개식 타고다. 수문장의 인솔 아래 궁 주변을 순찰하던 교대군이 궁성문에 도착한다. 의식을 위한 모든 준비를 완료한다. 엄고의 북소리가 울린다. 두 수문군의 가운데로 감독관에 해당하는 녹색 단령 차림의 승정원 주서와 궁성의 기물과 열쇠를 관장하는 액정서 소속의 사약이 나온다. ‘군호 응대!’ 하는 힘찬 울림이 퍼지면 양군의 참사가 군호를 확인한다. 군호는 서로의 신원을 확인하는 일종의 암호다. 병조에서 세 글자 이내로 국왕께 보고하면 승정원을 통해 내려온다. 승정원 주서가 동참하는 이유다. 승정원 주서가 수문장과 수문군에게 군호를 알려준다. 일말의 긴장감이 맴돌면서 관람객들이 의식의 절도를 느끼는 순간이다. 이어 ‘초엄’ 하는 참하의 외침에 따라 수문군들이 ‘초엄’을 복창하고 다음 의식이 이뤄진다. 교대의식의 첫 번째 절차를 알리는 신호로 나각과 나발 소리가 여섯 번 울린다. 주위를 환기시키는 신호다. 관람객들은 숨을 죽인 채 그들의 동작 하나하나를 지켜본다. 수문군과 관람객 사이에 따로 구분선이 있는 것은 아니다. 군악을 담당하는 취라척과 관람객은 최소한의 걸음만을 유지한 채 자리한다. 숨소리까지 다 들릴 만큼 가까운 거리다. 궁성문의 열쇠가 들어 있는 약시함의 인계가 이뤄지며 본격적인 수문장 교대의식에 들어간다. 수문군의 참하가 수문장에게 약시함을 전달하는데, 약시함에는 궁성문의 열쇠가 들어 있다. 열쇠가 가지는 상징성은 의식에도 고스란히 스며든다. 이 과정을 승정원 주서와 액정서 사약이 지켜본다. 개개의 동작은 유연하지만 절도 있다. 영국의 근위병 교대의식과 비교하자면 부드러움 속에 격식의 꼿꼿함을 숨기고 있다. 보는 이들도 좀 더 쉽게 다가선다. 참하의‘중엄’ 하는 외침과 수문군들의 복창, 드디어 교대 의식의 두 번째 절차가 시작된다. 이를 알리는 나각과 나발 소리가 세 번 엄고를 울리면 양 수문장들이 인사 후 부신을 맞추고 순장패를 인수인계한다. 부신은 두 조각으로 나뉜 나뭇조각인데 둘이 이빨을 맞춰 한 짝을 이룬다. 일종의 신분 확인서다. 마지막 절차는 ‘삼엄’이다. ‘향전’이라는 외침에 따라 수문군들이 자리를 이동해 얼굴을 마주하는 ‘면간’ 교대의식을 치른다. 수문장들에 이은 수문군간의 교대의식이다. 마지막으로 참하가 한 번 더 ‘향전’이라고 외치면 모든 절차가 끝난다. 교대를 마친 수문군은 숭례문까지 순라를 한다. 교대의식은 총 20분 정도 소요된다. 그리 오랜 시간이 걸리지 않아 지나가던 행인도 걸음을 멈추곤 한다. 이제는 서울에서 빼놓을 수 없는 의식으로 서울 시민들에게 많은 사랑을 받고 있다.

document_title: Changing of the Royal Guard at Deoksugung Palace
document_text:
[Place] Changing of the Royal Guard at Deoksugung Palace
[Category] Festivals/Events/Performances > Festivals
[Summary] The Changing of the Royal Guard is a re-enactment of the ceremony from the Joseon Dynasty (1392-1910) for changing the guards that protected and patrolled the royal palaces, and were in charge of the opening and closing of the gates to the palaces.
[Description] During the Joseon Dynasty, the royal guards were responsible for guarding and patrolling the gates of the capital city and the royal palaces. The royal palace guards, who were known as the "Wanggung Sumunjang", had the very important duty of protecting the king by guarding the entrance gates of the primary royal palace where the king resided. They were in charge of opening and closing the palace gates, inspecting all visitors, and maintaining a close surveillance of the palace. They were divided into day and night shifts, and the Changing of the Guard ceremony took place whenever the shifts changed over. In the late period of the Joseon Dynasty, the Changing of the Guard ceremony was conducted at Deoksugung Palace as at that time Deoksugung was the primary royal palace and the king then resided there. The Changing of the Guard ceremony was originally conducted at Gyeongbokgung Palace in the early Joseon period, but was moved to Deoksugung when Deoksugung was made the primary royal palace after Gyeongbokgung was burned down during the Imjin Invasions of 1592 - 1598.

document_text:

[Primary category] Festivals/Events/Performances

Palace in the early Joseon period, but was moved to Deoksugung when Deoksugung was made the primary royal palace after Gyeongbokgung was burned down during the Imjin Invasions of 1592 - 1598. After some extensive historical research, this splendid and elegant traditional Korean royal court cultural ceremony was first re-enacted in 1996 and has been a must-see among Seoul's tourist attractions ever since. This ceremony is a great opportunity to experience a rare traditional scene in Korea, as the ceremony is reenacted exactly as it used to be held, with guards wearing royal uniforms, carrying traditional weapons and playing traditional instruments. A tradition comparable to the Changing of the Guards at Buckingham Palace, this ceremony takes place three times a day in front of Daehanmun, the main gate of Deoksugung at 11:00, 14:00, and 15:30 p.m. (except for on Mondays). The Changing of the Royal Guard at Deoksugung starts with two mounted soldiers leading the way, and a total of 78 Sumungun making an appearance, led by the Sumunjang in the order of Sumunjang, Sumungun, Sungjeongwon Juseo, Aekjeongseo Sayak and Chwiracheok. Once all the Sumungun have arrived with the drumbeat of the Chwiracheok (a military band), it marks the beginning of the changing ceremony.

[설명] 1994년 서울정도 600년 기념행사로 시작하여 올해 21회를 맞이하는 ‘조선시대 과거제 재현행사’는 공정경쟁을 통해 인재를 뽑는 선진적 제도이자 세계적으로 빛나는 한민족의 문화유산인 과거제를 널리 알리고, 시민들에게 우리 전통문화의 우수성을 되새길 수 있는 계기를 마련할 것이다. ‘조선시대 과거제 재현행사’는 한시 백일장 형태로 진행되며, 세종실록오례의 가례 문과전시의를 토대로 원형에 따라 실시된다. 과거시험 후에는 급제자를 발표하는 방방례(放榜禮), 급제를 축하하는 은영연(恩榮宴)이 경희궁 과장에서 재현되며, 급제자가 국왕(뮤지컬배우 남경주 특별출연)이 내린 어사화를 쓰고 행진하는 ‘유가행렬(遊街行列)’이 행사의 마지막을 장식할 것이다. <2014년도 제 21회 조선시대 과거제 재현행사 과시생 모집> - 일시: 2014. 10. 5(일) 10:30~17:00 - 장소: 경희궁 - 모집인원: 선착순 200명 - 응시자격: 제한없음(전국)/ ※단 1회~20회 장원급자는 제외 - 시험내용: 한시(漢詩_七言律學) - 접수기간: 2014. 9. 12(금)~10. 2(목)/ ※신청기간 중 응시인원 접수 초과 시 해당일 접수분까지만 인정 - 접수 방법: 직접방문, 우편, 인터넷 접수/ ※과거제 행사 당일 현장접수 불가, 반드시 접수기한내 가급적 인터넷 접수 바람

[설명] 남산 팔각정에서 매일 15시에 봉수군들이 우리 국토를 방위하기 위하여 연마하였던 전통무예와 우리민족의 흥이 담긴 민속공연 등 다양한 전통문화공연( 장창ㆍ기창 등 창술시범, 제독검ㆍ본국검ㆍ예도 등 검법시범, 대나무 및 짚단베기 시범, 맨손을 사용하는 권법시범) 이 진행됩니다. 전통무예는 고대 수렵시대에는 궁사를 중심으로 수렵기술이나 전투에 의해서 발달되었으며, 농경생활이나 종교생활과도 밀접한 관계를 갖고 있어 각종 경기나 무속 예법 등에 도입되어 발달하였습니다. 우리나라의 경우 조선시대 문존무비 사상으로 발달을 보지 못하다가 임진왜란을 계기로 무예의 필요성을 깨닫게 되어 중국으로부터 여러 무예가 도입되었습니다. 1594년(선조27) 명나라의 장수 이여송으로부터 장창 등의 무예 6기가 도입되고, 영조 때 새로이 죽장창 등의 12기가 들어와 십팔기가 되었으며, 정조 때 기예 등의 6기를 더하여 24기가 완성되었고, 이를 <무예도보통지>에 수록하였습니다. 무예24기는 조선시대 무과시험의 과목으로 구한말 구식군대가 해체될 때까지 군인들이 다루던 군사무예였습니다.

[요약] 2015년 싱그러운 새 봄을 맞아 서울대공원에서는 4월 1일(수)부터 5월 6일(수)까지 36일간「봄, 꽃을 깨우다!」를 주제로 온실식물원 및 야외에서 봄꽃 축제를 연다.
[설명] 2015년 싱그러운 새 봄을 맞아 서울대공원에서는 4월 1일(수)부터 5월 6일(수)까지 약 한 달간 「봄, 꽃을 깨우다!」를 주제로 온실식물원 및 야외에서 봄꽃 축제를 연다. 서울대공원은 이번 축제를 통해 호접난, 덴파레, 긴기아넘, 온시니움, 심비디움 등 화려한 서양난 10종 1,500본과 홍대화금, 레티지아 등 진귀한 다육식물 70종 100본을 전시해 봄의 빛깔을 전달한다. 라벤더, 타임, 파인애플세이지, 렘쓰이어(양의 귀를 닮은) 등 허브식물 20종 2,000본 또한 함께 전시된다. 서울대공원 온실식물원은 높이 26m, 총 2,825㎡의 대형 실내 식물원으로 사막, 열대, 온대, 지중해성 식물이 전시되어 있다. 건조한 환경에서 자라는 선인장과 다육식물, 온대성 기후의 상록활엽수, 열대림에 사는 관엽식물, 지중해성 허브식물 등 880여종 8,000여본의 식물이 상시 전시되어 있다. 온실식물원 주변에는 튜율립, 펜지, 물망초, 금잔화, 종이꽃 등 싱그러운 봄의 전령들이 관람객을 맞을 준비가 되어 있다.

[Place] Dano Festival
[Category] Festivals/Events/Performances > Festivals
[Summary] Dano is one of the three major traditional holidays in South Korea, together with Seollal and Chuseok.
[Description] Dano is one of the three major traditional holidays in South Korea, together with Seollal and Chuseok. The holiday originated from the Mahan Confederacy, a confederation of Korean states that existed more than 2,000 years ago. Also called Surit-nal, it is celebrated on the fifth day of the fifth month of the lunar calendar. This year it falls on Thursday, June 1. On Dano, women traditionally wash their hair in water boiled with sweet flag, and men wear iris roots around their waist. Tteok (rice cakes) made with herbs are also eaten on this day. You can experience Dano and its related customs at the Namsangol Hanok Village or at the National Folk Museum of Korea. A variety of events are scheduled, including washing hair with sweet flag, making bows, fans, and kites, tasting herb rice cakes, riding swings and more.
[Opening hours] June 1 9:00~17:00
[Admission fee] Free ~ 5,000 KRW
