[Place] National Meteorological Museum of Korea
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities
[Summary] It is the first meteorological science and history museum that researches and preserves the meteorological culture of Korea from the Joseon Dynasty to modern times. The museum owns the world's last surviving rain gauge instrument, known as the Rain Gauge of the Chungcheonggamyeong Provincial Office, Gongju, invented 200 years earlier than the West.
[Description] It is the first meteorological science and history museum that researches and preserves the meteorological culture of Korea from the Joseon Dynasty to modern times. The museum owns the world's last surviving rain gauge instrument, known as the Rain Gauge of the Chungcheonggamyeong Provincial Office, Gongju, invented 200 years earlier than the West. The Seoul Meteorological Observatory (52 Songwol-gil, Jongno-gu, Seoul), where the National Meteorological Museum was established, is the center of Korea's modern and contemporary meteorological history. The modern meteorological observation started in Wonnam-dong, Gyeongseong, in 1907 and moved to Songwol-dong via Nakwon-dong. The building at the time of its establishment in 1932 and extension in 1939 have been maintained and served as the Korea Meteorological Administration until the administration moved to Dongjak-gu, Seoul, in 1998. For this continuity, it was selected as a ‘100-year observatory’ by the World Meteorological Organization in 2017.

[Place] Yongsan Park Partially Open Site
[Category] Nature
[Summary] The site was a previous residence for US military officers. It was named 'Sobinggo' during the Joseon Dynasty because ice was stored nearby.
[Description] The site was a previous residence for US military officers. It was named Sobinggo during the Joseon Dynasty because ice was stored nearby. It is now called Yongsan Garrison, including the site of the U.S. Army officers' quarters. Still, the American soldiers stationed in Yongsan right after the defeat of Japan did not call it Yongsan Garrison but Camp Sobinggo. From the Liberation to the Korean War, it was called Camp Sobinggo, but after the ceasefire agreement was reached, it was named Yongsan Garrison when the 8th US Army moved in.

[Place] Jamsildaegyo Bridge
[Category] Culture > Landmarks
[Summary] Located between Jayang-dong, Gwangjin-gu, and 27 Jamsil-dong in Songpa-gu, Seoul, it is the 6th bridge in Seoul built on the Han River. It was named Jamsildaegyo Bridge because of its connection to Jamsil-dong.
[Description] The bridge between Jayang-dong, Gwangjin-gu, and 27 Jamsil-dong, Songpa-gu, was named Jamsildaegyo Bridge because of its connection to Jamsil-dong. Construction began in October 1970, and the sixth bridge in Seoul was built on the Hangang River in July 1972. It was a six-lane bridge at first, with a width of 25m, and in 2003, it expanded and re-opened as an eight-lane bridge. An underwater weir was installed on the Jamsildaegyo Bridge to maintain the water of the Hangang River at a constant level. It solved problems such as changes in the ecosystem caused by the reflux of seawater and aesthetic issues caused by exposure to river structures.

[설명] 어린 날의 꿈과 희망으로 가득 찬 어린이대공원은사실 역사의 아픔을 간직한 곳입니다 . 이곳은 본래 조선의 마지막 왕 순종의 비 ( 妃 ) 인 순명황후 민씨의 능을 모신 공간이었습니다 . 하지만 일제강점기에 능은 다른 곳으로 옮겨지고 일본인을 위해 만들어진 골프장이 해방 이후에도 이어졌습니다 . 어린이대공원 ‘ 꿈마루 ’ 는 골프장을 이용하는 방문객을 위한 우리나라 최초의 ‘ 클럽하우스 ’ 였습니다 . 어린이대공원이문을 연 직후 ‘ 꿈마루 ’ 는 교양관에서 식당 , 전시관 , 관리사무소 등으로 수차례 모습을 바꾸었습니다 . 이후 ‘ 꿈마루 ’ 는 재생 건축의 대가 조성룡 , 최춘웅 건축가의 손에 의해 한국 근현대건축물을 대표하는 본래의 모습을 되찾게 되었습니다 . 덧붙인 흔적들을 지우고 , 북카페와 피크닉정원 등의 프로그램을 채워 다시 어린이들의 ‘ 꿈 ’ 을 담는 공간으로 재탄생했습니다.

document_title: Kkummaru(Dream Park) in Children's Grand Park
document_text:
[Place] Kkummaru(Dream Park) in Children's Grand Park
[Category] Nature
[Summary] A Place Where the Past, Present, and Future of Seoul Coexist, Kkummaru(Dream Park) in Children's Grand Park
[Description] This park, filled with thedreams and hopes of childhood, is actually a place that holds a painfulhistory. This place was originally where the tomb of Empress Sunmyeong, thewife of Sunjung, the last king of the Joseon Dynasty, was enshrined. However, the tomb was moved to another location during the Japanese occupation, while a golf course was built for the Japanese and remained even after liberation. Kkummaru (Dream Peak) in Children's Grand Park was Korea's first "clubhouse" for tourist visiting Korea. After the opening ofChildren’s Grand Park, Kkummaru wasused for different purposes such as an academic hall, exhibition space, andsuperintendent’s office. Later, Kkummaru was able torecover its original structure that was iconic of Korea’s modern andcontemporary architecture through the hands of famous renovation architects,Cho Sung-ryong and Choon Choi. They erased the superimposed layers and filledthe building with programs for a book cafe and picnic area to reintroduce it asa space to help children dream again, hence the kkum (dream) part of the name.
[Tags] KkummaruDream-Park-in-Childrens-Grand-Park

[Description] LCDC SEOUL was built where anauto repair shop and a shoe manufacturing factory once existed. A building wasadded to the existing two factory buildings to recreate the space into a culturecomplex. It's hard to find any traces of the old auto shop, but the dark grayconcrete walls wrapping around LCDC SEOUL still blend seamlessly into thesurrounding industrial landscape. You start the morning with asweet dessert and cup of tea in the first floor cafe, move up to the second andthird floor for different cultural experiences, and reach the bar on the fourthfloor around sundown for a drink. document_title: Kim Joong-up House of Architectural Culture
document_text:
[Place] Kim Joong-up House of Architectural Culture
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities
[Summary] Harmony Between East & West, Kim Joong-up House of Architectural Culture
[Description] Built in the 1970s, this two-story detached house was remodeled in 1986 by Kim Joong-up, who added exotic elements to every corner of the house based on traditional Korean architecture. This is a place where you can get a glimpse of the housing culture of the middle class at the time, and was designated as a Seoul Future Heritage in 2017. The KimJoong-up House of Architectural Culture harmoniously integrates Korean and Western architectural styles. The second-floor living room has an umul-maru , rafter structure, and windows covered with changhoji paper, which are mainly used in hanok , but with a modern interpretation. In contrast, the bathroom was designed in a European style. The dry bathroom with a dressing room attached, something that wasn’t common in Korea during the '70s and '80s, has a vintage jade-colored interior that stands out. Stepping out to the elegantly decorated garden, a water element, a characteristic of Kim Joong-up's architecture, is located on one side of the yard. Even equipped with its own small greenhouse, the Kim Joong-up House of Architectural Culture contains immense nature in the garden.

[Place] Songjeong Jebang gil
[Category] Nature > Natural Sites(Rivers)
[Summary] A riverside trail along Jungnangcheon that is beautiful in all four seasons
[Description] Songjeong Jebang gil is located along Jungnangcheon, extending from Seongdong Bridge to Gwangnaru gil Jebang. It is famous as a cherry blossom viewing spot in spring, a green shaded walkway filled with cicada sounds in summer, and a colorful foliage path in autumn. It has been selected by the city of Seoul as one of the top 220 summer green roads and one of the top 93 autumn foliage roads, and is known as a walking path along the water. [Place] Bamseom Island
[Category] Nature > Natural Sites(Parks)
[Summary] An island located downstream of the Mapodaegyo Bridge on the Hangang River, where the Seogangdaegyo Bridge passes through
[Description] Bamseom is an island located downstream from Mapodaegyo Bridge on the Hangang River, intersected by Seogangdaegyo Bridge. Known as a habitat for migratory birds, Bamseom gets its name from its chestnut-like shape. In the past, the island was inhabited. Still, during the development of Yeouido, the island was split into Upper Bamseom and Lower Bamseom after an explosion forced residents to relocate to Mapo-gu. The upper part of Bamseom, with its bay-shaped shoreline, became an important bird nesting area. Over the next 20 years, sediment from the Hangang River allowed trees and grasses to flourish, attracting birds and establishing the island as a well-known urban bird sanctuary. Bamseom Island is now approximately six times larger than it was originally. In 1999, it was designated as a Natural Ecosystem Conservation Area; in 2012, it was recognized as a Ramsar Wetland. While direct access to the island is prohibited, Bamseom Island can be viewed from Bamseom Park.

[Place] Ktown4u COEX
[Category] Culture > Other Cultural Destinations
[Summary] The No.1 K-POP spot for people worldwide, Korea's largest K-Culture complex facility
[Description] Ktown4u COEX is a K-Culture complex cultural space located in COEX, Samseong-dong, Gangnam-gu, a densely populated area. Visitors can experience Hallyu culture through collaborations with K-POP and in various fields such as beauty, fashion, and lifestyle. On the 2nd floor, SQUARE is a permanent store that sells products based on K-Culture. It primarily offers the latest released K-POP albums, goods, magazines, various Hallyu lifestyle items, clothing, and beauty products. The 3rd-floor Academy is an experiential space open to everyone who loves K-POP. It offers unique tourist experience programs, including one-day classes where participants can experience K-POP artists’ dance and vocals. The 4th floor, SPACE, is where K-POP artists and fans can interact directly. It hosts themed pop-up events, such as artist comeback events, dramas, art exhibitions, and more.

[요약] 종묘 서쪽 담장을 따라 길게 뻗은 고즈넉한 돌담길
[설명] 종묘 돌담길은 세계문화유산으로 선정된 종묘의 서쪽 담장을 따라 길게 뻗은 고즈넉한 돌담길입니다. 우리에게 이미 익숙한 역사문화명소인 북촌과 인사동 등과는 다르게, 최근 들어 새롭게 떠오르고 있는 골목입니다. 정갈하고 단아한 돌담을 따라 천천히 걸으며 주변의 카페와 공예작업실 등을 천천히 구경하기에 좋은 산책로이며, 골목 골목 한옥을 개조한 상점과 카페를 볼 수 있습니다. 고풍스러운 돌담과 울창한 나무가 어우러져 사계절 내내 아름다운 경관을 선사합니다. 특히 봄에는 벚꽃과 새싹이 돌담을 감싸며 화사한 분위기를 자아내고, 가을에는 단풍이 물든 돌담길이 그림처럼 펼쳐져 낭만적인 산책을 즐기기에 좋습니다. 이곳은 번잡한 일상에서 벗어나 여유롭게 산책하기 좋은 장소로, 전통 건축미와 자연이 조화롭게 어우러진 모습이 마음을 차분하게 만들어 줍니다. 종묘돌담길은 한국 전통문화의 흔적을 느끼며 사진을 찍기에도 훌륭한 포토 스팟입니다. 또한, 길을 따라 걸으면 인근의 창경궁, 창덕궁, 인사동과 삼청동 같은 전통과 현대가 어우러진 명소들도 함께 둘러볼 수 있어 다양한 문화 체험을 즐길 수 있습니다.

[Place] Jongmyo Shrine Stonewall Path
[Category] History > Historical Sites
[Summary] A serene stone wall path stretches along the west wall of Jongmyo Shrine
[Description] The Jongmyo Shrine Stonewall Path is a tranquil walkway that stretches along the western wall of Jongmyo Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Unlike well-known historical and cultural spots like Bukchon and Insadong, this pathway is a hidden gem that has recently gained popularity. Strolling along the pristine, elegant stone wall, visitors can leisurely explore nearby cafes, craft studios, and shops and cafes housed in renovated hanok buildings along the side alleys. The path is beautifully framed by the historic stone wall and lush trees, offering scenic views throughout the seasons. In spring, cherry blossoms and fresh leaves embrace the wall, creating a bright and cheerful atmosphere. In autumn, the wall is transformed into a picturesque setting draped in warm hues, perfect for a romantic walk. This peaceful spot offers an ideal escape from the busy pace of everyday life. Traditional architecture and nature are in harmonious balance, providing a calming ambiance. Jongmyo Stone Wall Path is a fantastic photo spot for capturing traces of Korea’s traditional culture. Walking along the path, visitors can conveniently explore nearby attractions, such as Changgyeonggung Palace, Changdeokgung Palace, Insadong, and Samcheong-dong, where tradition meets modernity, allowing for a well-rounded cultural experience.

document_text:
[Place] Seoul Museum of Art Buk Seoul Branch
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Art Museums/Galleries
[Summary] A cultural communication space where the museum and park meet, and people, nature, and art live and breathe together
[Description] Opened in 2013, the Buk Seoul branch of the Seoul Museum of Art is the first and largest branch of the Seoul Museum of Art. As a contemporary art space representing northern Seoul, it is a cultural landmark where art and everyday life naturally meet. It was designed as a cultural communication space where the museum and park come together, and where people, nature, and art live and breathe in harmony. Reflecting the place name Nowon, which is derived from the meaning 'Reed Hill', the museum is located on a small hill that appears to bring the beautiful natural scenery of Suraksan and Bulamsan, once hidden behind apartment complexes, into the heart of the city. All exhibitions, except for special exhibitions, can be viewed free of charge, making it a beloved and accessible destination for tourists as well.

[설명] 아티스트에게는 꿈의 무대이자 관객들에게는 특별한 즐거움을 선사하는 공간으로, 1,766석 규모의 뮤지컬 전문 공연장 신한카드홀과 1,379석(스탠딩 2,800석) 규모의 다목적 공연장 SOL트래블홀로 구성된 국내 최대 공연장입니다. 티켓 예매는 인터파크 웹사이트를 통해 간편하게 예약할 수 있습니다. 그 외에도 트렌디한 전시행사 공간 NEMO, 나만의 서재와 카페가 함께 어우러진 고품격 문화공간 북파크 라운지, 탁 트인 남산 전망으로 이국적인 정취를 풍기는 카페 필로스, 공연의 여운을 와인과 함께 곱씹을 수 있는 정통 레스토랑 스테이지B, 오리엔탈 푸드 전문점 솔로스키친도 함께 운영하고 있습니다.

[Place] BLUE SQUARE
[Category] Culture > Performance Halls
[Summary] A must-visit performance venue for musical fans
[Description] BLUE SQUARE is Korea’s largest performing arts complex offering artists a dream stage and audiences unforgettable experiences. It houses the 1,766-seat Shinhan Card Hall, dedicated to musicals, and the SOL Travel Hall, a multipurpose venue with 1,379 seats (plus a standing area that can accommodate 2,800 people). Tickets can be easily booked via the Interpark website. In addition to performances, BLUE SQUARE also features NEMO, a trendy exhibition space; Book Park Lounge, a premium cultural space featuring a café with reading areas; Café Philos, offering a striking unobstructed view of Namsan Mountain; Stage B, a fine-dining restaurant ideal for savoring a glass of wine after a show; and Solos Kitchen, specializing in Asian cuisine.
[Tags] BLUE SQUARE, musicals, performance venue, exhibitions, international shows in Korea, performances, shows, Book Park Lounge, Café Philos, Stage B, Solos Kitchen

[카테고리] 쇼핑 > 전문매장/상가
[요약] 작은 민화박물관 같은 이태원 숨은 명소
[설명] 대성표구사는 50 년째 이태원에서 역사를 이어오고 있는 가게입니다 . 대성표구사 1 대 대표는 인사동에서 표구를 배우다가 1971 년 이태원에 정착해 가게를 시작하였습니다 . 70~90 년대에는 미군 부대와 외국 대사관에 그림을 판매하였고 , 미국 등지에 족자와 병풍 등을 수출하기도 하였습니다 . 최근에는 2 대 대표와 가게를 함께 운영하고 있으며 , 단골들도 한국문화에 관심이 많은 외국인층으로 넓어졌습니다 . 가게 안으로 들어서면 멋스러운 민화와 풍속도 등 다채로운 그림들이 자리하고 있어 부담 없이 들어가 구경해볼 수 있습니다 .

[Place] Lee Frameshop
[Category] Shopping
[Summary] A hidden gem of Itaewon like a small folk painting museum
[Description] Lee Frameshop(Daesung Pyo Gusa) has been operating in Itaewon for 50 years. The first owner of Lee Frameshop studied frame in Insadong before settling in Itaewon in 1971 and starting the shop. In the 70s and 90s, he sold paintings to US military units and foreign embassies, and exported stools and folding screens to t h e US and other countries. In recent years, the shop has been run by the second generation of the family, and its clientele has expanded to include foreigners interested in Korean culture. When you enter the shop, you will find a variety of colorful paintings, including folk paintings and folk customs, so feel free to take a look around.

[설명] 경동시장은 전통과 현대가 조화를 이루는 서울의 대표 시장으로, 농산물부터 약재, 수산물까지 다양한 품목을 만날 수 있는 살아 있는 문화의 장으로 외국인 관광객들도 즐겨 찾는 명소입니다. 1960년 6월 개설된 농산물 전문시장으로, 산야에서 채취한 특산물을 중심으로 다양한 농산물을 합리적인 가격에 제공하며, 서울 도심 속 대표적인 전통시장으로 자리 잡았습니다. 1985년 경동 빌딩이 준공되어, 국내 최대 규모의 인삼시장과 한약 전문 상가가 형성되면서 약재와 인삼 분야에서 대구 약령시를 능가하는 전문성과 규모를 갖추게 되었습니다.

[Place] Gyeongdong Market
[Category] Shopping > Traditional Markets
[Summary] A representative market of Seoul in Cheongnyangni where tradition and modernity harmonize
[Description] Gyeongdong Market is one of Seoul’s iconic traditional markets, located in Cheongnyangni, where tradition and modernity coexist. It is a vibrant cultural hub offering a wide range of goods including agricultural products, medicinal herbs, and seafood, and is a favorite destination among foreign tourists. Established in June 1960 as a market specializing in agricultural goods, it has grown into a central traditional market in Seoul, offering a variety of mountain-harvested specialties and produce at reasonable prices. In 1985, with the completion of the Gyeongdong Building, the market expanded to become home to Korea’s largest ginseng and herbal medicine specialty zone, surpassing even Daegu Yakryeongsi in expertise and scale.

[장소명] 리피트랩
[카테고리] 쇼핑
[요약] 리피트랩은 빈티지 리바이스 데님과 다양한 업사이클 제품들을 만날 수 있는 공간
[설명] 리피트랩은 빈티지 리바이스 데님과 다양한 업사이클 제품들을 만날 수 있는 공간입니다. 오래된 데님과 빈티지 소재를 활용해 새로운 가치를 담은 제품들을 선보이고 있습니다. 처음엔 리피트(REPEAT)라는 이름으로 시작했으며, 예전 것들을 반복(repeat)해 또 다른 의미로 재탄생시킨다는 뜻을 담았습니다. 이후 더 다양한 작업과 실험을 시도하기 위해 ‘랩(LAB)’을 더해 리피트랩이라는 공간을 완성했습니다. 매장에는 다양한 빈티지 리바이스 청바지들이 사이즈별로 깔끔하게 진열되어 있어, 고객들이 손쉽게 원하는 제품을 찾을 수 있습니다. 빈티지 데님 특유의 감성과 정돈된 진열이 돋보이며, 클래식한 리바이스 데님부터 희소성 있는 특별한 아이템까지 다양하게 만나볼 수 있습니다. 리피트랩은 단순한 판매 공간을 넘어 빈티지 데님을 사랑하는 이들이 자유롭게 둘러보고, 입어보고, 자신에게 딱 맞는 스타일을 찾을 수 있는 아늑하고 특별한 매장입니다.

document_title: The replica of an old mayor’s office
document_text:
[Place] The replica of an old mayor’s office
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Others Cultural Facilities
[Summary] The office space of past Seoul mayors, including the furniture and office equipment from that time period, has been faithfully reproduced.
[Description] The Reconstructed Former Mayor’s Office is a workspace used by former mayors of Seoul for over 60 years, from the post-liberation period until May 2008. Located at the center of the 3rd floor of the Seoul Metropolitan Library, this space comprises a planning room, reception room, and office, featuring faithfully restored furniture and office equipment from that time.
[Tags] TongTongTour, SeoulMayor, CityHall, Mayor’sOffice, SeoulLibrary
[Address] 110 Sejong-daero, Jung-gu, Seoul (Seoul Library 3rd floor)
[Subway information] Subway Lines 1 / 2  City Hall Station  Exit 5,  53m
[Opening hours] Every Tue-Sun, 09:00-18:00  (Closed on Mondays and public holidays)
[Important note] The Reconstructed Former Mayor’s Office captures Seoul's history and records, replicating the Mayor’s Office, Reception Room, and Planning Situation Room of the former Seoul City Hall. This office space was used by successive mayors of Seoul for over 60 years, from the post-liberation period until May 2008.

Former mayors handled critical city affairs in the office, and the reception room welcomed important visitors to Seoul. The Planning Situation Room served as the heart of city administration, where the mayor, city officials, experts, and citizens received reports, deliberated, and made decisions on various agendas.

Originally located at the eastern end of the 3rd floor of the old city hall, it has now been reconstructed in the Secretary’s Office. Visitors can experience an immersive exhibition featuring administrative artifacts, including the original desk and chair used by the mayors and various gifts received from notable guests.

document_title: SeMA Public Space Project 《The Dance That Crosses Forever》
document_text:
[Place] SeMA Public Space Project 《The Dance That Crosses Forever》
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities
[Summary] An installation exhibition that breathes fresh vitality into linear spaces, embodying cycles and balances where center and end, inside and outside, continuously shift.
[Description] The Seoul Museum of Art presents its 2025 Public Space Project featuring world-renowned artist Ernesto Neto, who has broadened the horizon of contemporary sculpture. His new work Ba Ka Ba, The Dance That Crosses Forever is a large-scale installation traversing the lobby and open areas of the Seosomun Main Building. The work is crafted by crocheting industrial cotton fabrics in brown, reminiscent of tree trunks and night, and in pink, symbolizing flowers and day, filled with locally sourced guava leaves and tea tree leaves. The spirit of Brazil’s Neo-Concrete movement—emphasizing sensory engagement, participation, and subjective experience—finds new life in Neto’s work within today’s urban spaces, extending the possibilities of art. The SeMA Public Space Project 《The Dance That Crosses Forever》 aims to present a venue where art awakens the senses in everyday life, as city and museum converge.
[Venue] Lobby, Seosomun Main Building, Seoul Museum of Art

[Place] Ttukseom Hangang Park X Game Zone
[Category] Culture > Leisure/Sports Centers
[Summary] X-game Zone where you can enjoy skateboarding, inline skating
[Description] The X-Game Area at Ttukseom Hangang Park is a dedicated space for skateboards, inline skates, and BMX bikes. It features a spacious area with flat surfaces, jumps, slanted rails, and various other obstacles for free use. There are also side tracks accessible to everyone, making it suitable for beginners. If you want to try a unique sport in Hangang Park, this is the perfect spot. Occasionally, professional competitions are held here, filling the park with sports excitement throughout the year. Remember to wear protective gear such as helmets and knee pads when using the park. The X-Game Area is exclusively for skateboards, aggressive inline skates, and BMX bikes.

[Place] Chungmuro Station
[Category] Culture > Cultural Districts
[Summary] A station located in Chungmuro, once called the mecca of Korean cinema.
[Description] Chungmuro Station is a transfer station for Subway Line 3 and Subway Line 4. Since the 1950s, Chungmuro had been known as the mecca of Korean cinema due to the concentration of film production companies and theaters. Although the old theaters have gradually disappeared into history and the Chungmuro era has faded, its proximity to Myeongdong and Euljiro, which are visited frequently by young people and foreign visitors, is giving new life to the area once shaped by the film industry. With the harmony of traditional shops and new establishments, Chungmuro is now frequented not only by the middle aged but also by the younger generation.

[설명] 커버낫(COVERNAT)은 밀리터리, 아웃도어, 워크웨어 등의 빈티지웨어에서 얻은 모티브를 현대적인 소재와 룩으로 푸는 컨템포러리 브랜드입니다. 2008년에 데뷔한 이래 지금도 매 시즌 과거로부터 얻은 영감을 커버낫만의 시각으로 재해석해 좋은 만듦새를 기본으로 고객에게 "입는 즐거움"을 선사하기 위해 트렌드를 고민하며 다양한 캐주얼 스타일을 풀 컬렉션으로 소개합니다. 홍대 플래그쉽 1층에서는 ‘커버낫 우먼라인'을 만나볼 수 있는 쇼룸으로 구성되어 있습니다. ‘클로버하트’ 로고를 활용한 디스플레이와 오브제 등 감각적인 공간 속에서 편안한 쇼핑 및 착용이 가능하여 '입는 즐거움'을 만끽하실 수 있습니다. 지하 1층은 유니섹스 스토어로 의류, 모자, 신발, 가방 등 토탈 패션 아이템으로 구성된 공간입니다. 매 시즌 신상 아이템들을 한 자리에서 만나볼 수 있습니다. 커버낫 홍대 플래그쉽에서는 중국인 관광객을 위한 알리페이 결제가 가능하며, 외국인 관광객에 한하여 상품 구매 후에는 카운터에서 부가세 환급 또한 받을 수 있습니다. 주변에는 복합문화공간인 KT&G 상상마당이 있으며, LEE(리), What it isn't(와릿이즌), FALLET(팔렛) 등 유행을 선도하는 패션 브랜드들이 밀집되어 있어 트렌디한 홍대 패션 거리를 만나볼 수 있습니다. 지하철 2호선 홍대입구역 9번 출구에서 나와 도보 10분 거리에 위치해 있습니다.

[Place] Gongneung-dong Dokkaebi Market
[Category] Shopping > Traditional Markets
[Summary] Gongneung-dong Dokkaebi Market originated from street vendors gathered near Hwarangdae
[Description] The Gongneung-dong Dokkaebi Market originated from street vendors who gathered near Hwarangdae Station when the Gyeongchun Railway opened on July 25, 1939. Named for its fleeting nature, like a goblin's visit, the vendors would quickly disappear at the sign of a crackdown and reassemble snugly along the tracks to rebuild the market once things were clear. This traditional goblin market is the precursor to today's Gongneung-dong Goblin Market. Since then, the market has operated as a quintessential neighborhood market in Nowon-gu, as if a goblin's magic wand has made every possible item available. It offers a variety of products including livestock, groceries, restaurants, miscellaneous goods, and agricultural products. The market draws a steady stream of visitors due to its high-quality goods sold at affordable prices. Since 2019, it has been growing into an eastern landmark cultural tourism market, concurrent with the development of the Gyeongchun Line (Railroad) Forest.

[설명] ‘서울 왕궁수문장 교대의식’은 서울시가 주최하는 대표적인 전통문화재현 행사로, 조선시대 궁궐 문을 지키던 수문군의 교대 장면을 실감 나게 되살린 프로그램입니다. 수문장은 종6품의 관직으로, 수문장청 소속 참하와 수문군과 함께 궁문을 지키고, 출입을 단속하며 순찰을 수행했습니다. 교대의식은 실제 역사자료에 근거해 구성되었으며, 조선 후기 덕수궁을 중심으로 전개됩니다. 행사는 매주 월요일을 제외한 주 6일, 오전 11시와 오후 2시에 덕수궁 대한문 앞에서 열립니다. 일반 시민과 외국인 관광객의 흥미를 더하기 위해 다양한 체험 프로그램도 함께 운영되는데, ‘개식타고 체험’은 북을 직접 두드리며 의식 시작을 알리는 체험이고, ‘나도 수문장’은 수문장 복장을 입고 역할을 체험하는 프로그램이며, ‘전통복식 체험’은 조선시대 의상을 입고 사진을 남길 수 있는 인기 체험입니다. document_title: Deoksugung Palace Seoul Royal Guard Changing Ceremony
document_text:
[Place] Deoksugung Palace Seoul Royal Guard Changing Ceremony
[Category] Festivals/Events/Performances
[Summary] A traditional cultural reenactment event that realistically revives the changing scene of the royal guards who guarded the palace gates during the Joseon Dynasty.
[Description] The ‘Seoul Royal Guard Changing Ceremony’ is a representative traditional cultural reenactment event hosted by the Seoul Metropolitan Government, which realistically revives the changing scene of the royal guards who guarded the palace gates during the Joseon Dynasty. The royal guard commander (Sumunjang) was an official of the junior 6th rank, who, along with the subordinate officers (Chamha) and guards (Sumungun) belonging to the royal guard headquarters (Sumunjangcheong), guarded the palace gates, controlled access, and conducted patrols. The changing ceremony is structured based on actual historical records and unfolds centering on Deoksugung Palace in the late Joseon Dynasty. The event is held six days a week, excluding every Monday, at 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM in front of Daehanmun Gate at Deoksugung Palace. To add to the interest of general citizens and foreign tourists, various experience programs are also operated. The ‘Gaesiktago (Opening Drum Beating) Experience’ is an experience where one directly beats a drum to announce the start of the ceremony. ‘I am also a Royal Guard Commander’ is a program where one experiences the role while wearing the royal guard commander's uniform.

[Description] Located in Songpa-gu, Seoul, Saemaeul Traditional Market is a popular destination near Jamsil Baseball Stadium. It attracts many visitors before and after baseball games. [Place] Cheongdamdaegyo Bridge
[Category] Culture > Landmarks
[Summary] Korea’s first double-deck bridge, featured in films and animations
[Description] Cheongdamdaegyo Bridge, the 17th bridge over the Hangang River, connects Jayang-dong in Gwangjin-gu and Cheongdam-dong in Gangnam-gu. It holds the distinction of being Korea’s first double-deck bridge, with the lower deck serving Subway Line 7 and the upper deck accommodating motor vehicle traffic. Other notable double-deck bridges in the country include Yeongjongdaegyo Bridge connecting Seoul and Incheon International Airport and the Gwangandaegyo Bridge in Busan. Cheongdamdaegyo Bridge gained global attention as a filming location for Avengers: Age of Ultron and also appeared in the animated feature KPop Demon Hunters.

[Place] Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Others Cultural Facilities
[Summary] A space honoring the independence activist Woodang Lee Hoe-young, his five brothers, and their comrades.
[Description] Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall is a space honoring the independence activist Woodang Lee Hoe-young, his five brothers, and their comrades. This house is one of the early 20th-century Western-style buildings constructed by Westerners who entered Seoul, along the hills of Hongpa-dong, Sajik-dong, and Haengchon-dong in the Seodaemun area. Reborn as the Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall, this house possesses rich historical backgrounds and values even from an architectural history perspective. To remember its significance together, the Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall gave this old Western-style building the nickname 'The Old House on Sajik-dong Hill' while reshaping the site. Mr. Lee Hoe-young devoted himself to the anti-Japanese independence movement, contributing his entire family wealth to establish the Shinheung Military Academy. At the Lee Hoe-young Memorial Hall, encounter the history of the independence movement expressed with modern aesthetics, alongside the stories of the finest family of the Joseon Dynasty, the greatest revolutionaries of Joseon, the people who turned darkness into light, and the people who turned orchid leaves into blades.

[Place] Yongmasan Skywalk Observatory
[Category] Culture > Landmarks
[Summary] An extraordinary experience that feels like walking above the forest, offering a panoramic view of both the Seoul cityscape and the woodland.
[Description] Yongmasan Skywalk Observatory is an observatory facility created along Section 4 of the Seoul Dulle Trail (Mangwoo and Yongmasan) to allow visitors to enjoy both the forest and the city at a glance. It is constructed as a wooden deck structure with a maximum height of ten meters, enabling visitors to walk approximately one hundred sixty meters above the forest. From the observatory, visitors can appreciate the landscape of Seoul’s mountain ridges and the urban scenery stretching from Namsan N Seoul Tower to Bonghwa Mountain, Dobong Mountain, and Bukhansan. In addition, a variety of tree species and garden elements have been added around the observatory, allowing visitors to enjoy a diverse landscape.

document_text:
[Place] Choansan Neighborhood Park Barefoot Loess Trail
[Category] Nature > Natural Sites(Parks)
[Summary] A healing space to enhance the well-being of city residents weary from daily life
[Description] The Barefoot Loess Trail at Choansan Neighborhood Park opened in September 2024. It features a round-trip course of 134 meters, offering visitors a chance to relax in nature. This is the first trail in Seoul to incorporate a ground-spray cooling fog system, which helps maintain the texture and quality of the loess, allowing for a more pleasant walking experience. In addition to the barefoot trail, the park also includes a loess foot bath and a loess ball zone for a variety of wellness experiences. To ensure user convenience, the site provides a foot-washing station, sitting wall blocks for resting or putting on and taking off shoes, and shoe storage facilities.

[설명] 한국미술의 폭 넓은 스펙트럼과 다양성이 돋보이는 갤러리 띠오(THEO)는, 2020년 영국과 미술 시장에서 경력을 쌓은 두 명의 디렉터가 국제적 전문성과 네트워크를 한국 미술계에 도입하기 위해 설립되었습니다. 세계 문화유산으로 지정된 선정릉 앞에 위치한 띠오는, 예술 장르에 관계 없이 젊고 재능 있는 한국 예술가들을 지원하고 그들의 작품에서 잠재력을 찾아내는 데 전념하고 있습니다. 한국의 예술가들에게 플랫폼을 제공하여 그들이 성장하고 발전할 수 있도록 적극적으로 지원합니다. 또한 띠오는 해외 작가들을 한국 및 아시아 작가들에게 소개하며, 국가를 넘어 세계의 문화 간 교류를 촉진하고 예술적 담론을 확장하기 위해 노력하고 있습니다. 현재까지도 띠오는 전 세계 다양한 작가들의 전시회를 개최하고 있습니다. 이곳은 도전적인 프로젝트와 예술가들의 우수성에 대한 헌신을 바탕으로, 예술가들이 함께 공존하고 번영할 수 있는 공간으로 나아갈 예정입니다.

[Description] Gallery THEO, known for showcasing Korean art's broad spectrum and diversity, was established in 2020 by two directors with experience in the UK and the international art market. They aimed to introduce global expertise and networks to the Korean art scene. Located in front of the UNESCO World Heritage site Seonjeongneung, THEO is dedicated to supporting young and talented Korean artists, regardless of artistic genre, and uncovering the potential in their works. The gallery actively provides a platform for Korean artists to grow and thrive. In addition, THEO introduces international artists to the Korean and Asian art communities, fostering cross-cultural exchanges and expanding artistic discourse beyond national borders. THEO continues to host exhibitions featuring diverse artists worldwide. It aims to create a space where artists can coexist and flourish, driven by a commitment to challenging projects and artistic excellence.

document_title: A Wardrobe of Imagination - E-Land Collection Special Exhibition
document_text:
[Place] A Wardrobe of Imagination - E-Land Collection Special Exhibition
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities
[Summary] The magnificent beginnings of global designers, from Alexander McQueen to Yves Saint Laurent.
[Description] We recall the moment of opening a wardrobe door. The time brushing past fabrics, the memories lingering on our fingertips, countless garments and stories, and small attempts accumulate to become a single legacy. This exhibition focuses on the unseen, initial moments before fashion is completed. It is a journey tracing how the smallest fragments of thought—an unfamiliar object, a passing landscape, a sudden imagination—are realized into a single garment. A single flower, a folded piece of paper, and a moment of light and shadow are reborn as wearable art through a designer's perspective. Through a carefully selected collection from the 500,000 authentic archives amassed by the E-Land Museum over 30 years, you can encounter the magnificent beginnings of global designers, from Alexander McQueen to Yves Saint Laurent, in one place.
[Venue] My Art Museum One Grove Branch

[Place] Changsin-Sungin Quarry Observatory
[Category] Culture > Cultural Districts
[Summary] In the era of Japanese colonial rule, the Changsin-dong quarry was active, and atop its peak lies an observation deck, offering breathtaking night views.
[Description] The quarry observatory is built atop the summit of Changsin-dong quarry, providing a panoramic view of the city and natural landscapes at a glance. During the Japanese colonial period, a quarry was located in Naksan, Changsin-dong, to supply stone for the exterior of large buildings such as the Government-General of Korea, the old Seoul Station, and the Bank of Korea. After the Korean War, the quarry's use was discontinued, but the quarry observatory was located where immigrants and refugees settled to form a village. From the quarry observatory, with nothing obstructing the view, you can enjoy the skyline of Seoul at a glance. The second floor houses a coffee shop (Café Nakta), and the third floor features an outdoor observation deck, allowing you to appreciate the scenery of Seoul's cityscape and nature from any vantage point. Especially renowned is the breathtaking view that unfolds alongside the sunset. Enjoy the best panoramic view, a reasonably priced cup of coffee, and homemade ggangjeong and Nakta rice cakes. Small music concerts featuring historical and cultural stories, exhibitions, and live guitar performances are held occasionally.

[Place] 2026 Sungnyemun Gate Guard Ceremony
[Category] Festivals/Events/Performances
[Summary] Breathing life into our proud cultural heritage embraced by the historical city of Seoul! The 'Sungnyemun Gate Guard Ceremony' guarding Sungnyemun.
[Description] Pasu (Guarding) refers to defending the capital city and was one of the important military ceremonies during the Joseon Dynasty. Defending the capital city was the most critical issue during the Joseon Dynasty, and it emerged as a serious problem, especially after experiencing the Imjin War (Japanese invasions) and the Byeongja Horan (Manchu invasion) during King Seonjo's reign. The Guard Ceremony is a military ceremony of the Joseon Dynasty that connects the capital gate opening and closing ceremony,opening and closing the gates at Injeong (curfew) and Paru (lifting of curfew), with the patrol ceremony. Considering its position and role within the central military system, it can be viewed as a ceremony no less important than guarding the royal palace.

[설명] 장희빈 우물터 일대는 조선시대 초부터 이궁(離宮)인 연희궁이 있어 예로부터 이곳은 궁말, 궁뜰, 대궐재와 왕실 최초의 뽕밭을 일궈 서잠실, 장희빈 우물이란 이름으로 전해지고 있습니다. 최초의 이궁은 정종 3년(1400), 정종이 아우인 태종에게 왕위를 선위 후 이 곳을 피궁으로 사용하여 세종 7년 (1425) 8월 연희궁이라 칭하게 되었으며, 이에 궁실관리들과 궁녀들의 사가가 있어 궁말 여러 곳에 우물들이 있었다고 하나 오늘날까지 그 명맥을 간직하고 있는 샘이 바로 "장희빈 우물"입니다. 그 후 숙종(1674-1720)때 폐비된 인현왕후를 뒤 이은 희빈장씨(1659=1701)가 폐서인의 몸으로 이 곳 사가에 잠시 머물 때 마셨던 우물로 전해지고 있으나 검증된 바는 없습니다. 그러나 연희동에서 오래 전부터 구전(口傳)으로 "이 우물은 장희빈이 마신 물" 이라고 옛 어른들이 대대로 가꾸어 오고 있어 우리동 보물찾기 사업으로 선정하여 복원하게 되었습니다.

document_title: Site of Concubine Jang Huibin’s Well
document_text:
[Place] Site of Concubine Jang Huibin’s Well
[Category] History > Historical Sites > Historical Sites
[Summary] Jang Huibin’s Well has been associated with Yeonhui Palace, a detached palace since the early Joseon Dynasty. It has been associated with palace grounds, courtyards and main buildings.
[Description] The area of the Site of Concubine Jang Huibin’s Well has been associated with Yeonhui Palace, a detached palace since the early Joseon Dynasty. It has been associated with palace grounds, courtyards, main buildings, and the royal family's first mulberry orchard. It has been passed down by the name Seojamsil, known as the Site of Concubine Jang Huibin’s Well. The first palace in this area was used as a refuge palace by King Jeongjong, who abdicated the throne to his younger brother, King Taejong, in the 3rd year of King Jeongjong's reign (1400). Later, in August of the 7th year of King Sejong's reign (1425), the palace was renamed Yeonhui Palace. It is said that there were wells in various places within the palace grounds due to the presence of palace officials and palace women. Among them, the preserved well is called the Site of Concubine Jang Huibin’s Well. During the reign of King Sukjong (1674-1720), Huibin Jang (1659-1701), who followed Queen Inhyeon, who was deposed, briefly stayed at this place as a concubine, but there is no proof she drank from the well. Over time, oral tradition in Yeonhui-dong has perpetuated the belief that "this well is where Huibin Jang drank water," upheld by generations of elders. Consequently, it was chosen for restoration as a part of the community's treasure-hunting initiative.
[Tags] JoseonDynasty, Yeonhui-dong, KoreanHistory, Palace

[Summary] A complex cultural space where Louis Vuitton's store, exhibition, restaurant, and cafe are harmonized in one place.
[Description] Located at LV The Place Seoul, Shinsegae The Reserve, Louis Vuitton Visionary Journeys Seoul was planned to commemorate Seoul, a city where heritage and innovation intersect. [Place] Suraksan Byeokung Valley
[Category] Nature > Natural Sites(Rivers)
[Summary] A valley near Seoul accessible by subway
[Description] On the southwestern side of Suraksan Mountain lies the stunning Byeokun Valley. The name Byeokun Valley originates from the inscription “Byeokun Dongcheon (碧雲洞天)” carved into a rock in the valley. The name was given because the spectacular white rock formations of Suraksan, exposed throughout the valley, blend with the ravine’s scenery in a way that resembles white clouds resting in the area. For those who enjoy hiking, a recommended course begins at Byeokun Valley and leads up to the summit of Suraksan. For those who prefer valleys over hiking, a well-maintained wooden deck along the stream provides a refreshing spot for a picnic.

[Place] Dongdaemun Stadium Memorial
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Museums
[Summary] A museum where you can reminisce about the history of Dongdaemun Stadium, which opened as Gyeongseong Stadium during the Japanese colonial period and was demolished in 2007.
[Description] In October 1925, Gyeongseong Stadium first opened to the east of the Seoul City Wall. Over the course of 82 years, during which its name changed to Seoul Stadium and Dongdaemun Stadium, this modern stadium remained in the same location, going beyond its original role as a stadium and sharing history with the rapidly changing Republic of Korea. The Dongdaemun Stadium Memorial covers the history of the stadium from Gyeongseong Stadium, to Seoul Stadium which became a space for post-liberation sporting matches and various events, and until its demolition in 2007 after being renamed Dongdaemun Stadium. Please reminisce about the history of Dongdaemun Stadium within the flow of modern and contemporary Korean history at the Dongdaemun Stadium Memorial, where you can vividly feel the historical significance and the sense of place of Dongdaemun Stadium and its surrounding areas.

[Place] Seoul Baekje Children's Museum

[Summary] The only children's museum in the Gangnam area that exhibits and educates about the ancient history and culture of Seoul's Han River basin
[Description] Seoul Baekje Children's Museum is the only children's museum in the Gangnam area that exhibits and educates about the fact that Mongchontoseong was the royal fortress of the ancient kingdom of Baekje, Seoul's 2,000-year urban history, and the ancient culture of the Han River basin. Seoul Baekje Children's Museum is affiliated with Hanseong Baekje Museum and reopened in May 2024. It displays various artifacts excavated from Pungnap-dong Earthen Fortification, Mongchontoseong, and Seokchon-dong Ancient Tombs, which were Baekje's royal fortresses. The site offers a range of educational programs and cultural events, allowing visitors to experience and appreciate Seoul's rich ancient history and culture firsthand.

[Summary] Seokguram Grotto is nestled halfway up Inwangsan Mountain, just below Chimabawi Rock, and can be reached via the Inwangsan Mountain Trail.
[Description] Seokguram Grotto is nestled halfway up Inwangsan Mountain, just below Chimabawi Rock, and can be reached via the Inwangsan Mountain Trail. Inside, you'll find the Three Buddha Statues, while the surrounding forest path features a Buddha statue and a Maitreya Buddha carved into the rocks. Above the main hall at Sanshingak Shrine, a large rock bears a painting of the Mountain Spirit and a tiger that guards Inwangsan. About 30 meters to the right of Seokguram, you can also visit the Cheonhyangam Hermitage. From Seokguram, you'll enjoy stunning panoramic views of Seoul, with Namsan Tower visible on the opposite mountain and, on clear days, even Lotte Tower. Below, Gyeongbokgung Palace and the Blue House come into view.

[설명] 경복궁 건천궁 서쪽에 위치한 전각입니다. 청나라에서 구매한 서양 문물 관련 4만 여 권의 서적들이 이곳에 보관되었고 고종의 서재로 주로 사용되었습니다. 이외에도 어진을 모시거나 외국 사신들을 접견하는 장소로 활용되었습니다. 과거에는 창덕궁 함녕전의 별당으로 지어졌으나 1891년에 경복궁으로 이전되었습니다. 2006년부터 시민들에게 공개되었고 과거에 있던 서적들은 현재 서울대학교 규장각한국학연구원과 한국학중앙연구원 장서각에서 보관하고 있습니다. 2016년, 집옥재를 도서관으로 꾸며 개방했습니다. 7,8월을 제외한 4월부터 10월까지 개방하는 곳이니 해당 기간에 경복궁에 방문하게 된다면 함께 둘러보기 좋습니다.

[Place] Gyeongbokgung Palace Jibokjae
[Category] History > Historical Sites
[Summary] A pavilion located to the west of Geoncheonggung in Gyeongbokgung Palace, used as King Gojong's study
[Description] This building is located to the west of Geoncheonggung in Gyeongbokgung Palace. It housed about 40,000 books on Western artifacts purchased from the Qing Dynasty and was mainly used as King Gojong’s private library. Additionally, it served as a venue for enshrining portraits of kings or receiving foreign envoys. Originally constructed as a secondary building of Hamnyeongjeon Hall in Changdeokgung, it was relocated to Gyeongbokgung in 1891. The building was opened to the public in 2006, and the books previously housed there are now kept at Seoul National University's Kyujanggak Institute for Korean Studies and the Jangseogak Archives of the Academy of Korean Studies. In 2016, Jibokjae was transformed into a library and opened to the public. It is open from April to October, except for July and August, making it a great place to visit if you're in Gyeongbokgung during this period.

[설명] 《유영국: 산은 내 안에 있다》는 한국 추상 미술의 선구자 유영국(1916–2002) 탄생 110주년을 기념하는 역대 최대 규모의 회고전이자, 서울시립미술관이 새롭게 선보이는 '한국 근대 거장전' 시리즈의 첫 번째 프로젝트입니다. 이번 전시는 미공개작을 포함한 회화, 부조, 사진, 드로잉 및 아카이브 170여 점을 통해 1935년 도쿄에서 시작된 추상 실험부터 생애 후반 심상 추상까지 60여 년의 화업을 총체적으로 조명합니다. 일제 강점기와 한국 전쟁, 압축 성장의 격동을 관통하면서도 추상이라는 당대의 아방가르드를 삶과 작품으로 실천했던 그의 회화는, 창작의 본질을 묻는 오늘의 시점에서 다시 한번 깊은 울림으로 말을 건넵니다.

[Summary] The largest retrospective to date commemorating the 110th anniversary of Yoo Youngkuk's birth and the inaugural project of the 'Korean Modern Masters Exhibition' series at the Seoul Museum of Art.
[Description] 《Yoo Youngkuk: A Mountain Within Me》 is the largest retrospective to date commemorating the 110th anniversary of the birth of Yoo Youngkuk (1916–2002), a pioneer of Korean abstract art, and the inaugural project of the newly presented 'Korean Modern Masters Exhibition' series by the Seoul Museum of Art. This exhibition comprehensively illuminates his 60-year artistic career, from his early abstract experiments in Tokyo in 1935 to his later introspective abstraction, through over 170 works, including previously unreleased paintings, reliefs, photographs, drawings, and archival materials. Penetrating the turbulence of the Japanese colonial period, the Korean War, and the era of rapid economic growth, his paintings, which practiced abstraction, the avant-garde of his time, in both life and art, speak to us once again with profound resonance from today's perspective, questioning the very essence of creation.
[Venue] 1st Floor, Seosomun Main Building, Seoul Museum of Art
[Tags] Yoo Youngkuk Solo Exhibition,  Yoo Youngkuk: A Mountain Within Me,  Mountain,  YooYoungkuk,  AMountainWithinMe,  SeoulMuseumofArt,  SeMA,  Seoul Museum of Art

[Place] My Friend Seoul, Seoul Gallery
[Category] Experience Programs > Other Experiences
[Summary] A complex cultural space where you can experience the future and present of Seoul.
[Description] 'My Friend Seoul, Seoul Gallery' is a complex cultural space created to share Seoul's vision and values with its citizens, located in the basement of City Hall in the center of Seoul. It has excellent accessibility to nearby attractions such as Gwanghwamun and Deoksugung Palace, and is also connected to City Hall Station and Euljiro 1(il)-ga Station, allowing tourists to comfortably stop by, enjoy various contents, and take a rest. Hall 1 of My Friend Seoul, which consists of a 1:1600 scale model of the entire map of Seoul, the media-interactive 'Play Hangang', and the 'Media Wall' screening media art, and Hall 2 of My Friend Seoul, consisting of a 2-meter diameter globe-shaped 'Media Sphere' and the 'World City Wall' showing the world's top 5 cities and Seoul, are popular spots where you can overlook the future of Seoul and Seoul within the world. Also, the 'Kids Lounge', a space for children that explains Seoul's policies through play, and the 'Performance Hall', where cultural performances are held and Haechi animations are screened, can be comfortably enjoyed by family visitors.

[Place] Choong Ang High School
[Category] Culture > Education Centers
[Summary] The first private high school located in Jongno-gu
[Description] It is the first private school in the Republic of Korea, established in 1908 during the Japanese colonial period to save and establish the country through education. The school actively participated in national movements such as the March 1st Movement during the Japanese colonial period, the June 1st Movement, and the Gwangju Student Movement. Monuments commemorating the March 1st Movement and the June 10th Movement are erected, allowing visitors to reflect on history. Additionally, the school is famous for its exotic architectural style and is a popular tourist destination, as it was a filming location for the drama “Winter Sonata.”

[Place] Changsin-dong's Cliff Village
[Category] Culture > Cultural Districts
[Summary] A village built around a rock cliff used as Korea's only quarry
[Description] Changsin-dong Cliff Village, located in Changsin 1, 2, and 3-dong in Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, has undergone various transformations over the years. It was a quarry village in the 1960s, a wooden village in the 1970s, a sewing factory in the 1990s, and finally a sewing village in the 2000s. It is situated around the rocky cliffs once used as the nation's only quarry. [Place] Dilkusha
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Others Cultural Facilities
[Summary] Dilkusha, a red-brick house signifying "a joyful heart" in Persian. A historic residence reflecting the lives of the Taylor family who built it a century ago, alongside the elegant narrative embedded
[Description] Dilkusha, meaning "a joyful heart" in Persian, is the historical name given to the residence of Albert W. Taylor and Mary L. Taylor. The Taylor family commenced construction in 1923 and completed Dilkusha in 1924. Following a devastating fire in 1926, the structure was rebuilt in 1930. After the Japanese colonial authorities deported the Taylor couple in 1942, the property was briefly managed by Albert's younger brother, William W. Taylor. In 1959, the house was purchased by lawmaker Cho Kyeong-kyu of the Liberal Party. However, following the forfeiture of his assets to the state in 1963, ownership of Dilkusha transferred to the government. Left neglected for decades, the property severely deteriorated and lost its original form. In 2005, Professor Kim Ik-sang of Seoile University located the estate at the request of Albert’s son, Bruce T. Taylor. In 2006, Bruce finally returned to his childhood home after 66 years, bringing Dilkusha back to public prominence.

[Place] Adellain Jewelry Studio
[Category] Experience Programs > Wellness
[Summary] An experiential traditional Korean craft-based workshop where you can make one-of-a-kind silver jewelry in Jongno, Seoul, where tradition and modernity blend.
[Description] Adellain Jewelry Studio is a one-day Korean craft experience workshop located in Jongno, Seoul, where traditional and modern cultures coexist. Visitors can experience traditional Korean craft techniques in a calm and comfortable studio environment and directly make one-of-a-kind silver jewelry. All classes are conducted as 1:1 personalized sessions with a professional jewelry designer, allowing even beginners with no prior craft experience to participate easily and enjoyably. By referring to over 250 sample designs, you can choose various forms of jewelry, not only silver rings but also bracelets, pendants, silver clay jewelry, wood rings, etc. Depending on the design, you directly select the thickness, texture, gemstones, engraving, and plating (optional) to complete your own artwork. All jewelry uses high-quality silver clay made of 99.9% pure silver. Completed works can be worn immediately on the same day or beautifully packaged for a gift. This experience, conducted amidst the historical atmosphere of Jongno, Seoul, provides a meaningful souvenir of a trip to Korea and long-remembered memories to overseas travelers, families, and solo travelers alike.
[Tags] OneDayClass,  TraditionalCulture,  Crafts,  GyeongbokgungPalace,  Insadong,  Jongno,  Ikseondong,  TraditionalExperience,  FamilyExperience,  SeoulTravel

document_text:
[Place] Louis Vuitton Visionary Journeys Seoul
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities
[Summary] A cultural journey to experience Louis Vuitton's travel, craftsmanship, and heritage
[Description] 'Louis Vuitton Visionary Journeys Seoul' is a cultural journey to experience Louis Vuitton's travel, craftsmanship, and heritage, serving as an immersive exhibition illuminating the brand's legacy. It is a space that unravels the philosophy of travel and the creative heritage that the Maison has continued for over 170 years into a single narrative. The story, starting from trunk production in 1854, introduces the journey of Louis Vuitton's development into a global cultural house through thematic spaces. Following the exhibition route leading from the 5th floor down to the 4th floor, the narrative of Louis Vuitton's creation and travel unfolds naturally. The exhibition consists of a total of 12 spaces, unfolding the brand's history starting with trunks, the origin of the monogram, the artisan's workshop, the evolution of iconic bags, and Louis Vuitton's cultural narrative expanded through art and design collaborations, music, and fashion, just like a single journey.
[Venue] LV The Place Seoul, Shinsegae The Reserve 5th-4th Floors

[Summary] The Gyeongchun Line (Railroad) Forest in Gongneung-dong, Nowon-gu, Seoul, once traversed by trains bound for Chuncheon
[Description] The Gyeongchun Line (Railroad) Forest in Gongneung-dong, Nowon-gu, Seoul, once traversed by trains bound for Chuncheon, captures a unique mix of historical and modern elements. In this area, the Gongneung-dong section has evolved into a lively area reminiscent of New York's Central Park. It is connected to the adjacent Gongneung-dong Dokkaebi Market and dotted with a growing array of cafes and pubs. Consequently, this area has earned the nickname "Gongtral Park," inspired by Gongneung-dong. It's also known as "Gyeongnidan-gil" (akin to Gyeongnidan-gil in Gongneung-dong). Traditionally, old railway lines converted into parks have their tracks removed, but what sets this place apart is the preservation of its original railway tracks.

[Place] Dongdaemun History Museum
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Museums
[Summary] A museum that retraces the history of the former Dongdaemun Stadium site.
[Description] The Dongdaemun History Museum was established as a space to retrace the history of the former Dongdaemun Stadium site by preserving and exhibiting buried artifacts excavated during the construction of the Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) and Dongdaemun History & Culture Park. In the past, this area was the eastern region of the Seoul City Wall, where fortress defense facilities and various military installations were deployed to overcome the geographical disadvantages vulnerable to defense. As a result of excavation investigations conducted in 2008-2009, the walls and bastions (Chiseong) of the Seoul City Wall, the Igansumun watergate, and building sites from the Joseon Dynasty ,which were presumed to have been destroyed during the park creation and stadium construction during the Japanese colonial period, were confirmed, and related artifacts were excavated in large quantities. Please confirm the history layered upon the former Dongdaemun Stadium site at the Dongdaemun History Museum.

[Place] Shina Memorial Hall
[Category] History > Historical Sites > Modern Architecture
[Summary] This place serves as a memorial to honor the founder, Jang Ki-bong and Shina Ilbo, after its forced closure.
[Description] Located in Jeong-dong, this building is notable for its uniquely stacked red bricks. It was constructed in the 1930s as a reinforced concrete building with one basement level and two above-ground floors. The structure, finishes, and facilities reflect its nearly 100-year history. Initially used as the Korean branch of the American sewing machine brand “Singer,” it was purchased by Shina Ilbo, Korea's first commercial newspaper, in 1963. Shina Ilbo expanded the building by adding the third and fourth floors in 1975, using it as an annex. Following the forced shutdown of Shina Ilbo, the building was transformed into a memorial to commemorate the founder, Jang Ki-bong, and the newspaper. Today, it houses various businesses, including memorial halls, a café, and boutique shops, on each floor.

[Description] Big Issue Korea is a non-profit social enterprise that publishes a magazine that develops solutions to help homeless, marginalized, and disadvantaged people positively transform their lives. If you walk around the streets of Seoul, you may often encounter homeless individuals selling Big Issue magazines. Through these sales, they earn a legitimate income to sustain their lives. [Summary] Seoul's oldest secondhand foreign bookstore
[Description] Itaewon Books, which has been around since 1973, is the oldest foreign used bookstore in Seoul. It was founded in 1967 by a U.S. military unit that collected and delivered used books to bookstores and operated a stall with leftover books. At the time, foreign books were rare, especially those in color. A few years later, in 1973, he opened his own bookstore, where he has remained for over 40 years. It mainly deals with used books in English and American languages, and its categories are as diverse as a large bookstore, including poetry, fiction, philosophy, psychology, travel, religion, dictionaries, and history. • This place has been selected as a 'Seoul Future Heritage'. Among Seoul's modern and contemporary cultural heritage, Seoul Future Heritage is a tangible and intangible asset that is worth passing on to future generations.( https://futureheritage.seoul.go.kr)

[Place] Kyungguksa
[Category] History > Religious Sites
[Summary] A temple located on the eastern foothills of Samgaksan (Bukhansan) in Jeongneung-dong, Seongbuk-gu
[Description] Gyeongguksa Temple, nestled on the eastern slopes of Samgaksan (now known as Bukhansan), is a historic temple founded in the late Goryeo period. Renowned for its scenic mountain surroundings and fresh spring water, it attracts many visitors. The temple complex has 17 buildings, including Geungnakbojeon (Hall of Supreme Bliss), Yeongsanjeon, Myeongbujeon, Gwaneumjeon, and Sibangseonwon. Geungnakbojeon houses the Amitabha Buddha triad, along with wooden Buddhist paintings (designated as Treasure No. 748), Shinjungtaenghwa, and Palsangtaenghwa. Sibangseonwon offers a weekly Sunday meditation session, and the temple also hosts temple stay programs at Hwanheodang and Manwoldang. As one of Seoul's significant temples, Gyeongguksa was frequently visited by former President Syngman Rhee. During his tenure as Vice President, Richard Nixon of the United States visited the temple and later described it as one of his most memorable experiences in his memoirs, even including a photograph of his visit.

[Description] Eungbong-dong, located in Eungbong-dong, Seongdong-gu, stands at about 95 meters and has long been renowned for its beautiful scenery. During the Joseon Dynasty, kings would release hawks here for hunting, which earned it the nickname Maebongsan Mountain (Hawk Mountain). The area was also home to Dongho Dokseodang, an educational site for scholars and pavilions like Hwanghwajeong and Yuhajeong. To the south of Eungbong was a storage facility for ice called Dongbinggo. Today, Eungbongsan is designated as a neighborhood park, attracting many visitors who enjoy Seoul’s sunsets and night views. The park also offers recreational facilities such as a children's park, rock climbing area, and badminton courts, making it an excellent spot for various activities.

[Place] SeMA Museum of Photography
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities
[Summary] Korea's first public photography specialized art museum opened after more than a decade of preparation
[Description] The SeMA Museum of Photography, newly opened in Changdong, Dobong-gu, Seoul, is a branch of the Seoul Museum of Art and the first and only public art museum in Korea specializing in photography, established after more than a decade of preparation. The museum plans to continue diverse activities to become a new center for photographic art in Korea and Asia through creative and experimental exhibitions and programs encompassing the entire photography culture and in-depth research, collection, and preservation activities. Notably, the museum is equipped with facilities where visitors can experience the influence and artistic value of photography, including exhibition halls, education rooms, darkrooms, a photo library, and a photobook café for educational programs covering all age groups. The architecture was designed by Austrian architect Mladen Jadric (representative of Jadric Architektur ZTGmbH) and 1990 Urban Architecture (representative Yoon Geun-ju), who visualized and implemented the pixel of photography, which is a picture drawn with light.

[Place] Changdeokgung Secret Garden
[Category] History > Historical Sites > Palaces
[Summary] A garden of a Joseon Dynasty located inside Changdeokgung Palace
[Description] The Secret Garden (Huwon) at Changdeokgung Palace, once used for royal entertainment and ceremonies, is a significant heritage site showcasing traditional landscaping. Covering around 446,943 square meters, this expansive royal garden still has restricted areas that remain inaccessible to the public. Historically, it was off-limits to commoners, reserved only for the Joseon royal family. Nestled against Maebong Peak of Bugaksan Mountain, the garden features several ponds, including Buyongji, home to Buyongjeong Pavilion, Aeryeonji, Jangbangji, and Banwolji. The arrangement of pavilions and buildings reflects traditional Korean architecture, demonstrating a masterful harmony between structures and nature.

[Description] The Gyeongbokgung Stonewall Walkway is a walkway that surrounds Gyeongbokgung Palace. Centered around Gwanghwamun, to the left is the west gate of Gyeongbokgung, Yeongchumun; to the north is the north gate, Sinmumun; and to the right is the east gate, Geonchunmun. The left side of the Gyeongbokgung Stonewall Walkway connects to Seochon, while the north connects to the Blue House. The right side leads to Bukchon and Samcheong-dong, where visitors can also explore the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art and the National Folk Museum of Korea. The path is well-maintained, perfect for a stroll while experiencing the changing seasons. Walking along the Gyeongbokgung Stonewall Walkway offers a unique view that changes with the weather, whether it's raining or snowing.

[Place] Cheongjeon Yi Sang-beom House
[Category] History > Historical Sites
[Summary] Yi Sang-beom’s House located in Nuha-dong
[Description] The house and studio of Cheongjeon Yi Sang-beom, an artist recognized for pioneering new directions in Korean Southern School painting, are located west of Gyeongbokgung in Nuha-dong. Built-in 1929, the Yi Sang-beom House is an urban hanok featuring an L-shaped main house and straight-line servant quarters. It is distinguished by its rare kitchen with a cool wooden floor. Yi lived in this small, renovated hanok in Nuha-dong for 43 years. In his studio, known as Cheongjeon Hwasuk, he produced many artworks and mentored exceptional students such as Bae Ryeom and Park No-soo.

document_title: A Stroll Through Records: Seoul’s Parks
document_text:
[Place] A Stroll Through Records: Seoul’s Parks
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities
[Summary] An exhibition exploring the history and transformation of Seoul's parks through records
[Description] The exhibition "A Stroll Through Records: Seoul's Parks" showcases over 90 related records, highlighting Seoul's green space policies, stories of its prominent parks, park records categorized by keywords, and photographs of Seoul's parks taken by residents. Part 1, "The Path of Seoul's Parks," showcases the historical evolution of Seoul's park and green space policies through various documents, blueprints, photos, and videos. Part 2, "Parks Through Records," delves into the histories of notable parks like Namsan Park and Hyochang Park, utilizing records preserved by the Seoul Archives. Part 3, "Park Records Through Keywords," investigates the history and policies of parks, focusing on themes such as children, ecology, and urban regeneration. Additionally, the exhibition features 20 photos collected from a public event, allowing residents to share their personal memories of Seoul's parks.
[Venue] 2nd Exhibition Hall, 2nd Floor, Seoul Archives

document_title: Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education Namsan Library
document_text:
[Place] Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education Namsan Library
[Category] Culture > Cultural Districts
[Summary] Seoul's first public library, the Namsan Public Library
[Description] Seoul's first public library, the Namsan Public Library, originally opened in 1922 as the Gyeongseong Municipal Library in Myeong-dong. Situated in the heart of Namsan, the current building was constructed in 1965 following a public design competition. It has since been recognized as a Seoul Future Heritage building. The library boasts a collection of invaluable resources, including three volumes designated as Seoul City Tangible Cultural Properties and 227 volumes of 30 registered cultural properties. With a collection of around 500,000 books, 16,000 non-book materials, and 800 serial publications, Namsan Public Library is committed to preserving and sharing knowledge. In collaboration with the National Library of Korea, it has created a digital archive of rare and valuable materials, including ancient books and East Asian texts. Additionally, the library serves as a specialized resource center for Seoul's residents, offering various programs designed to enrich their cultural and intellectual lives.

[Place] Seoul City Wall Museum
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Museums
[Summary] A museum that introduces the history and value of the Seoul City Wall, which was constructed to display the authority of Hanyang, the capital during the Joseon Dynasty, and to defend against external
[Description] The Seoul City Wall is a city-scale fortress heritage constructed to mark the boundaries of Hanseongbu, the capital of the Joseon Dynasty, to display the capital's authority, and to defend against external invasions. With an average height of about 5 to 8 meters and a total length of approximately 18.6 kilometers, the Seoul City Wall is a landmark of the historical and cultural city of Seoul, built upon Korea's unique fortification techniques and collective craftsmanship. Located in Heunginjimun Park in Jongno-gu, Seoul, the Seoul City Wall Museum is a cultural space equipped with permanent exhibition halls, special exhibition halls, a Seoul City Wall resource room, and a learning room, encompassing the history and culture of the Seoul City Wall from the Joseon Dynasty to the present. Please discover the history and value of the Seoul City Wall, spanning over 600 years, at the Seoul City Wall Museum.

[Description] The Seoul Science Museum, located in Hageo-dong, Nowon-gu, opened its doors for the first time in Seoul in 2017. It was established to enhance science and cultural facilities in the Gangbuk area, aiming to bridge the gap in science and culture among different regions and promote balanced development across Seoul's districts. [Description] Little China Town, the Chinatown in Myeongdong, centers around the Chinese Embassy and has been home to Chinese cuisine restaurants, Chinese elementary schools, and Chinese culture for over 100 years. It is considered the oldest Chinatown in South Korea. The Seoul Overseas Chinese School, located next to the Seoul Central Post Office, has been there since 1909, along with some imported bookstores, Chinese food specialty stores, Chinese product specialty stores, and currency exchange shops. The Hansung Chinese Association handles various tasks such as issuing and processing documents for the Chinese community. This Chinatown developed naturally and is not managed comprehensively. It is one of the places where you can feel an exotic atmosphere in the city.

[Description] Musinsa Store Seongsu @ Daelim Changgo is the third offline space presented by Musinsa, following Musinsa Store Daegu and Musinsa Store Hongdae. Preserving the original structure of the Daelim Changgo, which has been an iconic location in Seongsu for around 50 years, the space has been reborn as a minimalist venue focused on the essence, without unnecessary decorations. [Summary] The final headquarters of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea and the momentous historical site of the assassination of Baekbum Kim Gu.
[Description] Designated as Historical Site No. 465, Gyeonggyojang served as the operational headquarters of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea following national liberation and marks the solemn historical site where Baekbum Kim Gu passed away. [Summary] A charcoal kiln Jjimjilbang (Korean Spa) located in Sinchon, the heart of the city
[Description] This charcoal kiln, jjimjilbang (Korean spa) in Sinchon, is popular throughout the year. Featured in numerous Korean dramas and media, it attracts foreigners eager to experience jjimjilbang culture. Visitors can enjoy traditional snacks like sikhye (sweet rice punch), eggs, roasted rice cakes, and sweet potatoes cooked in the charcoal kiln. The facility includes Gamagol Charcoal Grill, which offers grilled pork belly, and Gamagol Korean Restaurant, which serves traditional Korean dishes perfect for a post-sauna meal. Additionally, it boasts a playroom for children, gaming consoles, a nail art station, and a sky garden for diverse entertainment options. A unique aspect of this jjimjilbang is the hearth room, where heated charcoal is placed in a brazier, providing direct warmth to guests.

[설명] 국립극장 대표 여름축제 <여우락 페스티벌>의 컴백! ‘여기 우리 음악(樂)이 있다’라는 뜻의 여우락 페스티벌은 우리 음악을 기반으로 하는 음악가들과 다양한 영역의 예술가들이 참여하는 페스티벌입니다. 2010년 첫 선을 보인 이래 한국을 대표하는 우리 음악 축제로 매해 여름을 뜨겁게 달구며 지금까지 약 8만 8천여 명의 관객과 '우리 음악'을 만났습니다. 여러 장르를 넘나드는 예술가들의 만남과 과감한 음악적 실험으로 우리 음악의 새로운 지평을 열어 온 여우락 페스티벌은 올해로 17주년을 맞이했습니다. 지금까지의 성과에 안주하지 않고 기존 축제와 차별화 된 변화를 시도하고, 페스티벌을 기다리는 많은 관객에게 또 다른 우리 음악 세계를 선보일 예정입니다. 이한철, 강산에X정보권, 선우정아X채지혜, 립제이X유희X박동석, 동양고주파X최예림, 하림X구이임, 삼산X서의철 가단, 상자루X안예은, 컨트리공방X정윤형, 김수인X리치맨과 그루브나이스, 김백찬X김반장과 생기복덕, 유태평양과 함께 올 여름, 우리 음악의 바다 위 12가지 섬에서 나만의 취향을 발견해 보세요!

[Place] 2026 Yeowoorak Festival
[Category] Festivals/Events/Performances
[Summary] This summer! Dive into the sea of our music! The National Theater of Korea's representative summer festival.
[Description] The comeback of the National Theater of Korea's representative summer festival, ! The Yeowoorak Festival, meaning ‘Here is our music (樂)’, is a festival participated in by musicians based on our traditional music and artists from various fields. Since its first showcase in 2010, it has heated up every summer as Korea's representative traditional music festival, meeting with approximately 88,000 audiences and 'our music' to date. The Yeowoorak Festival, which has opened a new horizon for our music through encounters with artists crossing various genres and bold musical experiments, celebrates its 17th anniversary this year. Not settling for achievements so far, it attempts changes differentiated from existing festivals and plans to present another world of our music to the many audiences waiting for the festival. This summer, discover your own taste on 12 islands over the sea of our music along with Lee Han-chul, Kang San-eh X Jung Bo-kwon, Sunwoo Jung-a X Chae Ji-hye, Lip J X Yoo Hee X Park Dong-seok, Dongyang Gozupa X Choi Ye-rim, Hareem X Gu I-im, Samsan X Seo Eui-chul Gadan, Sangjaru X Ahn Ye-eun, Country Gongbang X Jung Yoon-hyung, Kim Su-in X Richiman and Groove Nice, Kim Baek-chan X Kim Ban-jang and Saenggi Bokdeok, and Yoo Tae-pyung-yang!

[Summary] A billiard hall in front of Korea University, where not a single chair has been changed
[Description] The billiard hall is located in front of Korea University and has been in operation since it opened in 1967. [Place] Cheongwoon Literature Library
[Category] Culture > Education Centers
[Summary] Jongno-gu's literature-specialized library built in hanok style
[Description] Cheongwoon Literature Library is Jongno-gu's 16th library, built in hanok style, creating an attractive space for reading, contemplation, and rest. It houses a diverse collection of literary books, focusing on poetry, novels, and essays. Not only does it provide various reading group venues for residents, but it also operates curated exhibitions centered on domestic literary works and authors, as well as humanities lectures and poetry writing classes. This space, where you can feel the ambiance of hanok and nature, won the grand prize at the 2015 Korea Hanok Competition. We hope you will experience the charm of traditional Korean architecture and find solace in nature.

document_title: Seoul Metropolitan Archives Exhibition <A City’s Boarding Log>
document_text:
[Place] Seoul Metropolitan Archives Exhibition <A City’s Boarding Log>
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities
[Summary] An exhibition introducing the journey of Seoul’s transportation through archived materials. More than 120 records from the Seoul Metropolitan Archives and materials donated by an engineer who particip
[Description] Another story of records at the Seoul Metropolitan Archives The Seoul Metropolitan Archives presents the exhibition A City’s Boarding Log, introducing the journey of Seoul’s transportation. The exhibition traces the city’s growth from the aftermath of the Korean War to the 1980s, as it built the foundations of its transportation system through archival materials. It showcases more than 120 records owned by the Seoul Metropolitan Archives, as well as donated materials from an engineer involved in the construction of the subway, vividly conveying the atmosphere of that era. In addition, a new permanent space has been created by relocating and reconstructing the exhibition contents of the Seoul Archives and Culture Center on the third floor of the Seoul Metropolitan Library, allowing visitors to explore Seoul from multiple perspectives. Follow the traces of time along the roads of Seoul and reflect on the paths we have taken and those that lie ahead.
[Venue] Seoul Metropolitan Archives, 2nd floor, Exhibition Hall 1

[Summary] 2Gil29 Gallery, located in Garosu Gil
[Description] Located in the vibrant Garosu-gil area of Sinsa-dong, Gangnam, where diverse interests and dynamic Seoul culture converge, 2Gil29 Gallery has been actively introducing contemporary art to the public since its opening in 2015. The gallery has fostered active exchanges with prominent Korean artists such as Hong Jung-hee, Choi Sun-ho, Nam June Paik, Lim Young-kyun, and Kang Suk-young while also showcasing works by artists like Kwon Young-ho and Charlie Han to diversify the Korean art market. The gallery’s curatorial approach is based on a wide range of creative works, fostering a more positive and progressive discourse on art. Through deeper communication and interaction with art, it transcends mere visual and auditory engagement, offering meaningful aesthetic and spiritual exchanges with artists. This, in turn, enhances the value of their creative endeavors. In addition, 2Gil29 Gallery is committed to discovering and nurturing emerging talents such as upcycling artist Hong Ji-hee, singer-turned-painter Yoo Hyun-suk, and Kwon Jae-hyuk, a graduate of the University of the Arts London (UAL).

document_title: Seoul Archives Children’s Record Experience Room <Twisting Record Exploration>
document_text:
[Place] Seoul Archives Children’s Record Experience Room <Twisting Record Exploration>
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities
[Summary] A play-based experiential exhibition aimed at children aged 7 to 13 to easily understand records
[Description] The Seoul Archives has prepared an interactive exhibition for children, “The Twisting Record Exploration”, designed to help them easily and enjoyably experience records. The exhibition is divided into three main sections. Part 1, “From Memory to Record”, allows visitors to explore various methods of remembering, learn about recording tools, and understand different types of records. Part 2, “Record Exploration”, features an interactive experience where participants can examine records of Seoul and their records and even build landmarks based on the records held by the Seoul Archives. Part 3, “The Record Keepers”, introduces the roles of record researchers and preservation scientists who collect and preserve records. As a specialized public archive, the Seoul Archives not only collects and preserves Seoul's records and residents' memories but also strives to provide diverse record information services. We hope this children’s interactive exhibition will inspire more citizens to take an interest in records and actively participate in the documentation world.
[Venue] Exhibition Room 3, 2nd floor, Seoul Archives

[설명] 부루의 뜨락은 1978년 개업하여 현재까지 운영되고 있는 음반가게입니다. 영화와 드라마에도 장소가 등장한 명동의 명소이자 중고음반점의 대명사로 알려져 있습니다. 1층은 케이팝 음반과 굿즈, 2층은 재즈와 팝송CD, 3~4층은 클래식 레코드 판을 판매하고 있습니다. 약 10만장 이상의 음반 중에서 클래식 LP가 특히 많습니다. 잘 찾아본다면 1980-90년대 미국 흑인 뮤지션들의 희귀한 음반도 찾아볼 수 있습니다. 1990년대 들어 대중들의 취미활동이 변화하면서 음반 구매율이 줄어들기 시작했고, 일본 LP애호가들이 음반을 높은 가격에 사가기 시작하면서 이 시기부터 주 소비층이 외국인으로 바뀌었습니다. 1990년 후반부터 국내 음반판매점은 한류 가수들의 앨범을 일본에서보다 저렴하게 구입할 수 있어 한국을 찾는 일본인들에게 필수 관광코스로 각광을 받아왔습니다. 당시 회현지하상가를 중심으로 명동 일대에는 11개 음반가게들이 있었고 그 중에서 ‘부루의 뜨락’은 터줏대감 역할을 하였습니다. 현재에는 K-POP이 세계적으로 알려지면서 동남아나 유럽에서 온 손님들이 음반을 찾는 경우도 있어 최대한 다양한 종류의 음반을 갖춰 놓게 되었습니다.

[Place] buruttrak
[Category] Shopping
[Summary] A record shop opened in Myeong-dong in 1979.
[Description] Buruttrak, established in 1978, is a long-standing record shop still in operation today. Known as a landmark in Myeong-dong, it has appeared in films and dramas several times. The first floor features K-pop albums and merchandise, the second floor sells jazz and pop CDs, and the third and fourth floors are dedicated to classical vinyl records. Within the vast collection of over 100,000 records, there is a particularly large selection of classical LPs. With some luck, you might also find rare albums by American Black musicians from the 1980s and 1990s. In the 1990s, as the hobbies of the Korean public shifted, record purchases began to decline. However, Japanese LP enthusiasts started buying records at high prices. During this period, the main customer base gradually shifted to foreigners. By the late 1990s, Korean record shops became essential tourist spots for Japanese visitors who could buy K-albums cheaper than in their country. Back then, the area around Hoehyeon Underground Shopping Center and Myeong-dong had 11 record shops, with 'Buruttrak' being a well-established figure. Nowadays, with K-pop's global popularity, the shop attracts customers from Southeast Asia and Europe, and it stocks a wide variety of records to meet diverse tastes.

document_text:
[Place] Joseon Yangban Hospitality Culture Experience Performance 'Onggi Concert'
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities
[Summary] A two-hour curated journey to experience the one-table-per-person hospitality culture of Joseon Yangban families while appreciating Pansori, traditional performing arts, and dance.
[Description] [Performance Introduction] The Onggi Concert goes beyond simple appreciation of traditional Korean music (Gugak); it is a 'participatory prestige Gugak performance' where the audience becomes the protagonist of the Sarangbang (reception room) elegance of the Joseon Dynasty. [Program Composition] ▶ Greeting (Approx. 10 minutes) A docent personally welcomes each audience member in the lobby. Upon entry, an individual table (dok-sang) — tea and refreshments on a traditional small dining table — is set, allowing you to experience the essence of the Yangban guest reception culture of the Joseon Dynasty. ▶ Explanation and Performance (Approx. 75 minutes) • Historical stories of the individual table culture, Dadam (tea conversation), and Gwangmudae (Docent explanation, approx. 15 minutes) • The 'Simcheong falling into the water' scene from the Pansori (Approx. 15 minutes) • Detailed explanation of the music and Chuimsae (exclamations) experience (Approx. 10 minutes) • The 'Blind Man Sim opening his eyes' scene from the Pansori (Approx. 15 minutes) • Q&A and conversation with the singer (Soriggun) and drummer (Gosu) (Approx. 20 minutes) ▶ Farewell (Approx. 10 minutes) Souvenir presentation, photo taking, and guestbook signing.
display_address: Gwangmudae, Traditional Performance Art Creation Maru, 9th Floor, New Building (Dong N), Dongdaemun Shopping Complex, 59 Cheonggyecheon-ro, Jung-gu, Seoul
