[Summary] A Place Offering Letter-Related Products and Services
[Description] "Glewol," a pure Korean word meaning 'letter,' is also used to honor the act of writing letters. Since 2019, Glewol has operated a letter shop in Seoul, offering a variety of letter-related products and services. The store aims to make letter writing a part of modern culture, continuing the value and spirit of writing letters. At the Glewol Yeonhui branch, you can experience a penpal service for a fee of 10,000 KRW, where you can exchange replies with someone you don't know. The cozy space is filled with various items such as stationery, postcards, and fountain pens. There is also a designated area where you can sit and write letters after purchasing your stationery, allowing you to enjoy the ambiance of Glewol while crafting your letters.

[Description] The Seoul Hiking Tourism Center (Bugaksan Mountain) is located on Samcheong-dong Cultural Street and offers a range of services for hiking tourists. Focused on Bugaksan Mountain, it provides Korean, English, Chinese, and Japanese information for different hiking trails in Seoul, including Bukhansan Mountain, Inwangsan Mountain, and Gwanaksan Mountain. Visitors can also access guidebooks and brochures about Seoul’s hiking tourism. [설명] 《어긋난 파동, 흔들리는 시간》은 우리가 흔히 '노이즈'라고 부르는 것 — 불규칙한 소리, 예측할 수 없는 변수, 시스템 밖으로 밀려난 것들 — 을 새롭게 바라보는 오민과 카밀 노먼트의 2인전입니다. 노이즈는 제거해야 할 방해물이 아니라, 오히려 그 안에서 새로운 관계와 의미가 태어나는 장소일 수 있습니다. 오민과 카밀 노먼트는 각자의 방식으로 이 질문에 답합니다. 오민은 아르코 다원예술 창작주체 지원사업의 일환으로 수년간 연구, 제작해 온 시간 기반 설치 〈동시〉 연작을 처음으로 한자리에서 보여주며, 국내 미술관 최초로 전시하는 카밀 노먼트는 사운드 설치 작품인 〈플렉서스(리좀) 서울〉을 아르코미술관의 커미션으로 선보입니다.

document_title: Untuned Time : Camille Norment, Min Oh
document_text:
[Place] Untuned Time : Camille Norment, Min Oh
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities
[Summary] An exhibition exploring the new meanings and possibilities of what we define as "noise"—elements that seamless order has long excluded within the overwhelming torrent of information.
[Description] 《 Untuned Time : Camille Norment, Min Oh 》 is a two-person exhibition featuring Camille Norment and Min Oh that sheds new light on what is commonly referred to as "noise," including irregular sounds, unpredictable variables, and elements pushed outside the boundaries of established systems. Noise is recontextualized not as an obstruction to be eliminated, but as a fertile ground where new relationships and meanings emerge. Camille Norment and Min Oh respond to this inquiry through their respective creative methodologies. Min Oh presents her time-based installation series, Simultaneous, displayed together in one place for the first time—a body of work researched and produced over several years as part of the Arko Multi-disciplinary Arts Support Project. Concurrently, Camille Norment marks her inaugural solo presentation at a domestic museum with Plexus (Rhizome) Seoul, a sound installation commissioned specifically by the Arko Art Center.
[Venue] Exhibition Halls 1 and 2, Arko Art Center
[Tags] Daehakro,  Kkumbat Theater,  Naksan Park,  Marronnier Park

[설명] 박선영전통한복연구실은 전통 한복의 정수를 담고 있는 곳으로, 이곳은 서울시무형문화재 제11호 침선장 박선영 장인이 한복의 아름다움과 그 속에 깃든 조상의 얼을 지키기 위해 시작되었습니다. 현재 이곳은 침선장 박선영 장인의 기술을 이어받은 그녀의 아들 김기상씨가 이어받아 운영하고 있습니다. 고객은 다양한 색감의 고급 원단 중에서 선택하고, 치수와 디자인을 결정하여 맞춤형 한복을 제작할 수 있습니다. 제작 기간은 약 7-10일이며, 국제 배송 서비스는 제공되지 않습니다. 이곳은 전통 한복에 대한 교육도 진행합니다.

[Description] Park Seon-yeong Traditional Hanbok Research is dedicated to preserving the essence of traditional hanbok. It was founded by Master Artisan Park Sun-young (Seoul's Intangible Cultural Heritage No. 11: Chimseonjang) who aimed to uphold the beauty of hanbok and the spirit of ancestors embedded within it. Currently, the studio is operated by her son, Kim Ki-sang, who has inherited her skills. The production period is approximately 7-10 days, and international shipping is not available. The studio also offers educational programs on traditional hanbok.

[Summary] An exhibition that recalls the old word 'love' once again through contemporary senses.
[Description] The 20th-anniversary exhibition of the Seoul Museum of Art's Nanji Residency, 《The Origin of Love (AMOR EX MACHINA)》, is structured as a journey to look back on the meaning of love by borrowing the archetypes of old stories in an era where technology rewrites relationships. Technology is no longer a tool placed outside of life, but has become an environment that conditions our senses and relationships. We wake up to smartphone alarms, move along paths indicated by satellites, and spend our days encountering news selected by algorithms. Within this, the ways we remember and form relationships are also changing. The exhibition proposes that our destination amidst the changing landscape of technology lies in love, the sense that makes us human.
[Venue] Exhibition Halls on the 2nd and 3rd floors, and Crystal Gallery, Seosomun Main Branch, Seoul Museum of Art

[Place] National Jeongdong Theater Cecil
[Category] Culture > Performance Halls
[Summary] The National Jeongdong Theater of Korea, Cecil, operates a 232-seat performance hall.
[Description] The National Jeongdong Theater of Korea, Cecil, is a historic performance hall in Jung-gu, Seoul. Originally opened in 1976 as Cecil Theater, it’s a small yet iconic venue with a capacity of 232 seats. During the late 1970s, it became the heart of Korea's theater scene, hosting the Korea Theater Festival from 1977 to 1980. Despite its prominence, financial difficulties led to its closure in 2018 after being operated by private theater groups 'Madan' and 'Rodem.' In April 2018, the Seoul Metropolitan Government spearheaded a cultural regeneration project to reopen Cecil Theater and handed its management to a non-profit organization. Designed by renowned architect Kim Joong-up, the theater has long been a cornerstone of Korean performing arts and cultural heritage. In 2022, the theater was revitalized under the management of the National Jeongdong Theater, taking on the new name 'National Jeongdong Theater of Korea, Cecil.' Today, it serves as a vibrant space for artists and audiences to connect through innovative and experimental performances, upholding its legacy and creative core values.

[Description] Newly established in Gwanghwamun Square, the Garden of Gratitude is a space designed to reflect upon the gratitude toward Korean War veterans and the achievements and prosperity of the Republic of Korea, which has transitioned from an aid-recipient country to a donor country. [Summary] The only traditional temple in the Dongjak-gu area, enveloped by Seodalsan Mountain.
[Description] Enveloped by Seodalsan Mountain, an important mountain forming the waist of the green axis connecting Bukhansan Mountain through Namsan Mountain to Gwanaksan Mountain, Dalmasa Temple is a sanctuary where you can enjoy the beautiful nature that changes with the seasons while overlooking the Hangang River and Namsan Mountain. [Place] BANKSY: Still Here
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities
[Summary] A symbol stronger than identity, Banksy's unending message!
[Description] The street artist Banksy, who operates while concealing his identity, is one of the world's most famous artists, yet his true identity remains shrouded in mystery. Nevertheless, people are captivated by the powerful messages he leaves on street walls. The exhibition <BANKSY: Here Still> introduces his artistic world through images and major projects that represent Banksy. By following works that contain messages of war and peace, satire and humor, as well as hope and solidarity, we aim to examine why so many people still discuss Banksy today. The questions posed by the anonymous artist remain ongoing. While his identity remains a mystery, the messages he left behind continue to live on beside us today.
[Venue] ALT.1, The Hyundai Seoul

[Summary] Anyangcheon Stream, where every season brings a new scenic walk
[Description] Anyangcheon Stream is a tributary of the Han River that flows through Anyang-si, Gwangmyeong-si, and the Seoul districts of Geumcheon-gu, Guro-gu, Yangcheon-gu, and Yeongdeungpo-gu, eventually joining the Han River west of Seongsandaegyo Bridge. Strolling along the Yangcheon Dulle-gil trail, you’ll discover a variety of charming sights and attractions. Highlights include the Anyangcheon Stream Embankment Cherry Blossom Road, the longest cherry blossom path in Seoul, as well as peaceful spaces like the Ecological Park, Family Garden, and Sports Park. In particular, you can enjoy seasonal scenery in the heart of the city along the Anyangcheon Stream : the Autumn Foliage Road (Anyangcheon Walkway) between Yangpyeong Bridge and Mok-dong Bridge, the Cherry Blossom Road between Mok-dong Bridge and Omokgyo Bridge, and the Anyangcheon Stream Ecological Plants Center between Sinjeonggyo Bridge and Ogeumgyo Bridge.

[설명] 2008년 서울시청 신청사 부지 조성 공사 과정에서 조선시대의 것으로 추정되는 유구와 유물이 다량 확인되어 발굴조사가 이루어졌습니다. 이곳에서는 근대와 조선시대에 조성된 호안석축(護岸石築)과 건물지 등의 유구와 함께 도자기, 동전, 기와 등 다양한 유물이 출토되었습니다. 특히 보물로 지정된 불랑기자포(佛狼機子砲)를 비롯하여 총통, 철환 등 조선시대 무기류도 다수 확인되었습니다. 옛 지도와 관련 자료를 조사한 결과, 서울시청 인근에는 조선시대 병기 제작을 담당하던 관청인 군기시(軍器寺)가 위치했던 것으로 파악되었습니다. 서울시청 부지는 과거 군기시의 일부였던 것으로 추정되며, 관련 유구를 보존하고 출토 유물을 전시하기 위해 군기시유적전시실이 조성되었습니다.

[Place] Gungisi Relics Exhibition Hall
[Category] Culture > Cultural Facilities > Others Cultural Facilities
[Summary] Exhibiting Gungisi relics and excavated artifacts from the Joseon Dynasty discovered during the construction process of the new Seoul City Hall.
[Description] During the site preparation construction process for the new Seoul City Hall in 2008, a large number of structural remains and artifacts presumed to be from the Joseon Dynasty were identified, leading to an excavation investigation. Here, various artifacts such as ceramics, coins, and roof tiles were excavated alongside structural remains like building sites and stone revetments constructed during the modern era and the Joseon Dynasty. In particular, many weapons from the Joseon Dynasty were identified, including Chongtong (gun barrels), Cheolhwan (iron cannonballs), and the Bullanggi Japo (breech-loading swivel gun) designated as a Treasure. As a result of investigating old maps and related materials, it was determined that Gungisi, a government office in charge of manufacturing weapons during the Joseon Dynasty, was located near Seoul City Hall. The Seoul City Hall site is presumed to have been part of the past Gungisi, and the Gungisi Relics Exhibition Hall was created to preserve related structural remains and exhibit excavated artifacts.
[Venue] B1 Floor, Seoul City Hall, 110 Sejong-daero, Jung-gu, Seoul

[Place] Tongui-dong Alley
[Category] Culture > Cultural Districts
[Summary] An alley located west of Gyeongbokgung Palace, where historical value is preserved
[Description] This alley, located west of Gyeongbokgung Palace, preserves historical value as a site related to Gyeomjae Jeong Seon and Chusa Kim Jeong-hui, where logistics movement and human exchange for Gyeongbokgung Palace were once active. During the Joseon Dynasty, great artists like Gyeomjae Jeong Seon and Chusa Kim Jeong-hui resided in Seochon. In modern times, notable artists, including painters Lee Jung-seop and Lee Sang-beom, and poets Yun Dong-ju and Yi Sang, were also residents. We hope you will enjoy exploring history and culture together in Tongui-dong Alley, where a cultural village has been established with various cultural and artistic spaces, such as the Boan Inn, where poets Yi Sang, Yun Dong-ju, and painter Lee Jung-seop once stayed.

[요약] 한지가헌 공간 및 전시 설명 도슨프 프로그램과 상설체험프로그램, 한지인화소 체험
[설명] 도슨트 프로그램: 전문적인 해설을 통해 한지가헌을 이해할 수 있는 가이드 투어입니다. 한지 문화 전반에 대한 이야기와 함께 각 공간의 의미를 이해 할 수 있는 프로그램입니다. 상설체험 프로그램: 전통한지를 활용하여 한지 기념품을 제작하는 상설 공예체험입니다. 계절에 따라 다양하게 기획되는 프로그램을 통해 한지의 다양한 물성을 경험할 수 있습니다. 한지인화소 (Hanji Print Studio): 공간에 비치된 QR코드로 사진인화를 신청하시면, 선택하신 한지에 사진을 인화해드립니다. 신청부터 인화, 건조까지 약 10분정도 소요되며 현장에서 바로 수령할 수 있습니다.
[태그] 한국공예디자인문화진흥원, 한지, 북촌한옥마을 명소, 안국역 명소, 한지가헌, 한지문화홍보관
[주소] 서울 종로구 북촌로 31-9 (재동, SWNA)
[지하철 정보] 지하철 3호선 안국역 2번출구, 355m
[이용 시간] 10:00-19:00
[이용 요금] 입장료 무료, 상설체험 및 도슨트 무료
[참고 사항] 한지인화소 한복 착용 시 무료인화 이벤트

document_title: Hanji House Docent Program/Permanent Experience Program/Hanji Print Studio
document_text:
[Place] Hanji House Docent Program/Permanent Experience Program/Hanji Print Studio
[Category] Culture > Other Cultural Destinations
[Summary] Hanji House Space and Exhibition Explanation Docent Program, Permanent Experience Program, and Hanji Print Studio Experience
[Description] Docent Program: A guided tour that provides professional commentary to help visitors understand the Hanji House. This program explains the culture of hanji and the significance of each space. Permanent Experience Program: This is a permanent craft experience program where you can make hanji souvenirs using traditional hanji. Through programs planned according to the season, you can experience the various properties of hanji. Hanji Print Studio: If you apply for photo printing using the QR code provided in the space, we will print your photo on the hanji of your choice. The process from application to printing and drying takes about 10 minutes, and you can pick up your photo on the spot.
[Tags] Hanji House,  Hanji Culture Promotion Center,  Korea Craft & Design Foundation,  Hanji,  Bukchon Hanok Village Landmark,  Anguk Station Landmark
[Address] 31-9 Bukchon-ro, Jongno-gu, Seoul
[Subway information] Subway Line 3 Anguk Station Exit 2, 355m
[Opening hours] 10:00-19:00
[Admission fee] Free admission, permanent experience, and docent tour
[Important note] Hanji Print Studio Free printing event when wearing hanbok
